conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Evidence Presents - Sinnott/enochian - Sinnott
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: Ah, the supposed language of the angels. I've not learned it. Never saw the need. I suspect the angels of creation can speak English just fine.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Evidence Presents - Sinnott/catacomb map - Sinnott
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I found this map of the catacombs underneath the manor...

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Evidence Presents - Sinnott/catacomb map - Sinnott
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: Did you, now? ...might I see it?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Evidence Presents - Sinnott/catacomb map - Sinnott
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: It seems self contained. Only two entrances, both that connect to the greater grounds.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Evidence Presents - Sinnott/catacomb map - Sinnott
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: Thank you for showing me this, my child.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Evidence Presents - Sinnott/catacomb map - Sinnott
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: No hidden ways out of there. I had hoped one path, at least, led to a wider complex...

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Evidence Presents - Sinnott/fetters - Sinnott
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: Well, typically, they are manacles used to restrain one around the feet.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Evidence Presents - Sinnott/fetters - Sinnott
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Can you tell me anything about fetters?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Evidence Presents - Sinnott/fetters - Sinnott
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: But given where we are, I suspect you mean it in the more... esoteric sense.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Evidence Presents - Sinnott/fetters - Sinnott
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: In which case, it is a term used to describe what anchors a spirit to a place - or person.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Evidence Presents - Sinnott/fetters - Sinnott
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: This manor houses many spectres, most likely trapped by the events that led to their death.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Evidence Presents - Sinnott/fetters - Sinnott
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: Perhaps they are fettered to the building or land. Perhaps something else keeps them trapped here...

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Evidence Presents - Sinnott/gauge - sinnott
speaker: Mister Ward
en: You've noticed the strange device in the atrium, I assume?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Evidence Presents - Sinnott/gauge - sinnott
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: Hmmm... I have seen it.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Evidence Presents - Sinnott/gauge - sinnott
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: I am told it tracks our readiness for the main event...

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Evidence Presents - Sinnott/gauge - sinnott
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: ...but I believe it tracks us.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Evidence Presents - Sinnott/reflection - Sinnott
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Are you okay, Father?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Evidence Presents - Sinnott/reflection - Sinnott
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: My mission is not complete but my part in it is over.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Evidence Presents - Sinnott/reflection - Sinnott
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: What happens next is up to you.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Evidence Presents - Sinnott/reflection - Sinnott
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: As for me, I have spent much of my life fighting the Demiurge's illusions.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Evidence Presents - Sinnott/reflection - Sinnott
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: Whatever comes after this, trick or not, I intend to let myself enjoy it while I can.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Evidence Presents - Sinnott/Doyle's gnostic bible- Sinnott
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Father, would you know what faith Mister Doyle follows?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Evidence Presents - Sinnott/Doyle's gnostic bible- Sinnott
speaker: Father Sinnott

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Evidence Presents - Sinnott/Doyle's gnostic bible- Sinnott
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: I am not sure what business it is of yours, child, but no - I do not know what faith guides him.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Evidence Presents - Sinnott/Doyle's gnostic bible- Sinnott
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: Not anymore.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you know much about the Marquess?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Blake
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: I know... some. Before coming here, I spoke with my protestant counterpart, Reverend Campbell. Due diligence and all that.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Blake
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: He mentioned the Marquess has changed in the years since his wife's passing. Not an uncommon thing.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Blake
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: Grief can make a man do strange things, and the Marquess largely shut himself off from the world. Once an ardent churchgoer, he rarely attends service now. He also closed off all of his wife's charitable donations.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Blake
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: And, of course, he has invited many heathens to his land to challenge God's order and allow them to speak with the dead. He's fallen a long way from the man Mary married.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Coventry
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you know much about Mister Coventry?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Coventry
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: No - he has a knack for speaking, but saying nothing.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on O Finn
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you know Mister Ó Finn?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on O Finn
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: Know him, no, but we have talked. It is always refreshing to learn how others perceive this reality.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on mantovani
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Did you speak with Miss Mantovani yet?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on mantovani
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: I have. I am fascinated by how she has managed to meld her more heretical beliefs with her Catholic faith.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on mantovani
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: Though, I gather such things are more common in Italy than here.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you talked with Miss Callaghan?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Fiadh
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: I have not. She seems intent on avoiding me, which I understand. I would not be surprised if her local priest speaks of her often and unkindly in his sermons.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Dupre
speaker: Mister Ward
en: How have you found Mister Dupré?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Dupre
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: We spent some time talking about death and what comes afterwards.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Dupre
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: He was polite but wary. Based on the stories I hear out of America, I do not blame him.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Darcy
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you talked with Missus D'Arcy?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Darcy
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: Only long enough to know that she should not be here - it will do her no good.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Father sinnot
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Tell me about yourself, Father.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Father sinnot
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: What could you want to know other than I am a priest? Do you want a list of hobbies?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Father sinnot
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Are you the local priest?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Father sinnot
speaker: Mister Ward

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Father sinnot
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: I am not. If I were, things would be different here.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Father sinnot
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: My parish is in Belmullet. A few days' walk north of here.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Father sinnot
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Did you... walk here?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Father sinnot
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: I did. If it were a good enough way for the Lord to get around, it would do me, too.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Father sinnot
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: The task at hand requires dedication, persistence, sacrifice, and clarity. The walk here helped me hone my mental fortitude.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Cathal
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you talked with Mister O'Meara?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Cathal
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: Endlessly. He is obsessed with angels - or what he takes be be angels, at least. He seems to think I have an interest in spending my days discussing this with him. He is wrong.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Hazel
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What do you think of Missus Erickson?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Hazel
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: We have not had much cause to speak, despite her following me around for many hours after my arrival on Wednesday.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Ettiene
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you know Mister Toussaint?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Ettiene
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: No, but I know his reputation as a debunker of charlatans, and I know that fire comes from mistreatment in his youth.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Ettiene
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: As a result, he does not make much time for priests...

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Arwa
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you met Miss Hisham, at all?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Arwa
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: I think she expected me to rain down fire and brimstone upon her and her faith.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Arwa
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: But I don't care. If she had been a Sufi, then we could have talked faith for there lies much overlap between how they and I see the world.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Arwa
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: She was not, so we talked archaeology instead. That seemed to break through the fog I've heard others mention.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Arwa
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: I hope she finds whatever she is looking for here. It might bring her mind some peace.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Ruairí
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you know Doctor Callaghan?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Ruairí
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: Hmmm? Ah, the witch doctor. Perhaps I am being unfair. I admire his willingness to try anything he thinks could help his patients.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Ines
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you spent any time with Miss Barbosa?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Ines
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: I have, but I would be remiss in my duties to share anything we discussed. She is a very devout woman.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Saoirse
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you talked with the cook, Miss Murphy?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Saoirse
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: I suspect that girl does not talk with anyone. She seems as if she is missing  a part of her soul.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Saoirse
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: ...Every confession, it seems as though she has something to ask of me. And yet, she does not.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Saoirse
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: She seems as if she is missing a part of her soul.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Ivy
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you talked with Miss McLeod?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Ivy
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: I have not. She does not have much to talk about with an old Catholic priest.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Varley
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Can you offer any insights into Mister Varley?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Varley
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: A devout man. I hope this event does not weigh too heavily on him.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Lan Fen
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you know Missus Lau?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Lan Fen
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: The chaperone? Not really, she and her partner have very little they need my guidance with.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Skerritt
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you know Mister Skerritt?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Skerritt
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: Our paths have very little reason to cross, so no.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Skerritt
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: I gather he is a... difficult man to be around, so I count that as a blessing.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Skerritt
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: But every soul is worth redeeming, even the less charitable ones.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you any opinion on Miss Quinn?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Corentine
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: There are some who visibly stiffen as I enter a room. When possible, I tend to give these people a wide berth...

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Caitlin
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Can you tell me anything about the housekeeper?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Caitlin
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: The very definition of a good Catholic woman. Confesses daily, absolving herself of sins so she can repeat them ad nutum.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Darragh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you dealt with Mister Hunter?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Darragh
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: Hmm. For a groundsman, he seems to lack a great deal of knowledge about the grounds.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Darragh
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: How does he not know the history of the place and what came before?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Darragh
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: Why does he seem so undisturbed by the land's inability for proper growth?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Darragh
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: He does not seem a dullard, so would he have reason to lie?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Seamus
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you met the porter, Mister Doyle?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Seamus
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: Of course. He took my bags to my room for me.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Walter Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you talked with young Master Blake?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Walter Blake
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: No, I gather the child stays away from people. Not that I would expect him to be introduced to me even if he weren't.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Deane
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you talked with Miss Deane recently?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Deane
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: Not at all. She is one of the guests I have not yet met.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Character Presents - Sinnott/Opinion on Deane
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: Though everyone else seems to have their little histories with her...

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Analysis Presents - (to) Sinnott/Unknown Vestments - Sinnott
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I don't recognise your vestments, Father - do they represent something of note?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Analysis Presents - (to) Sinnott/Unknown Vestments - Sinnott
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: For those with the eyes to see, they show all. For anyone else, they are just robes. I would not think too hard about it.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Analysis Presents - (to) Sinnott/Unknown Vestments - Sinnott
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I hope you are well, Father, you look... under the weather...

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Analysis Presents - (to) Sinnott/Unknown Vestments - Sinnott
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: I perhaps spend too much time indoors and underground.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Analysis Presents - (to) Sinnott/Unknown Vestments - Sinnott
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: When you reach my age, you will no doubt also carry your years on your face.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Analysis Presents - (to) Sinnott/Scarring - Sinnott
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Forgive my prying, Father, but you look as though you've been through the wars...

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Analysis Presents - (to) Sinnott/Scarring - Sinnott
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: Hmmm? Ah, my scars. Yes, I was a missionary in my youth. Foolish enough to think I could bring enlightenment to the masses through word instead of deed.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Analysis Presents - (to) Sinnott/Scarring - Sinnott
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Anywhere exotic?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Analysis Presents - (to) Sinnott/Scarring - Sinnott
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: Many places, Mister Ward, but do not be so arrogant as to think it's only the darkest parts of the map that need their eyes opened.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Analysis Presents - (to) Sinnott/Scarring - Sinnott
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: It is as hard to save a soul here in Ireland as anywhere else. Further away from the dark does not mean closer to the light.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Analysis Presents - (to) Sinnott/Unusual Cross - Sinnott
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Your cross, Father, it has an extra element - the circle behind it. What is the meaning, if I might ask?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Analysis Presents - (to) Sinnott/Unusual Cross - Sinnott
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: You may. It depicts the everlasting life of the immortal soul and represents my own personal flavour of beliefs.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Analysis Presents - (to) Sinnott/Unusual Celtic Cross - Sinnott
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Mister Doyle's cross looks quite similar to your own...

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Analysis Presents - (to) Sinnott/Unusual Celtic Cross - Sinnott
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: Yes. It does, doesn't it.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Analysis Presents - (to) Sinnott/bible - sinnott
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I don't recognise your bible, Father - what translation is it?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Analysis Presents - (to) Sinnott/bible - sinnott
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: It is an uncommon translation I picked up on my travels.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Analysis Presents - (to) Sinnott/bible - sinnott
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: Its focus? For those with the eyes to see, it shows all. I... would not think too hard about it.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Analysis Presents - (to) Sinnott/bible - sinnott
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What is the focus of your edition?

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Ward in room - Sinnott
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: My child... This is unacceptable. Please leave at once.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Ward in room - Sinnott
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: I'll let the manager deal with you. I've much more important things to be doing.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Post Quest - Sinnott
speaker: Mister Ward
en: The world can certainly be a callous place, but a ‘prison’ is a bit of a stretch.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Post Quest - Sinnott
speaker: Mister Ward
en: That sigil though… Father Sinnott seems convinced it was designed to kill an Aeon.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Post Quest - Sinnott
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Yet it looks so similar to those I’ve found throughout this house.

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Post Quest - Sinnott
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I assumed these sigils were some form of Irish pagan magic...

conversation: Cast/Lorcan Sinnott/Post Quest - Sinnott
speaker: Mister Ward
en: But then how did this one end up in Austria for Father Sinnott to find?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Fiadh conversation
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Ah, Hello. I don't believe we've met?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Fiadh conversation
speaker: Mister Ward
en: We have not. I'm Declan Ward. I arrived just yesterday, from Dublin. And yourself, Ma'am?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Fiadh conversation
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Fiadh - Fiadh Callaghan, no need for the formalities. I arrived at the hotel just a few days ago, but I've lived in the area all my life.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Fiadh conversation
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Ah, a local. A good person for a stranger to become acquainted to.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Fiadh conversation
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I'm not just local, I'm the local Bean Draoí, Declan, a wise woman. I've come to minimise the damage of this damnable séance.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Fiadh conversation
speaker: Detective Ward
en: LEAVE

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Fiadh conversation
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I'll let you go.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Fiadh conversation
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: You take care now, Declan, and don't forget to get a bite to eat into you. It's going to be a long day.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Fiadh conversation
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Ah Declan, aren't you fierce good coming back to see me.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Fiadh conversation
speaker: Mister Ward
en: We have not. I'm Declan Ward. I arrived just the day before yesterday, from Dublin. And yourself, Ma'am?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Fiadh conversation
speaker: Detective Ward
en: CONFRONT!

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Fiadh conversation
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Take these components and bring them to the well. Maybe you'll see what I'm missing. May the gods be with you - because they are surely counting on you.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Fiadh conversation
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Well... You're not wrong. I'd do anything to keep this land safe.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Fiadh conversation
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: This lot shouldn't be doing their séance, but I doubt I can stop them.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Fiadh conversation
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Best I can do is protect the land against them.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Fiadh conversation
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Charms and spells should do it...

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Fiadh conversation
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: ...and yet they aren't enough. I can't figure it out.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Fiadh conversation
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I'm at my wit's end, Declan Ward.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Fiadh conversation
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I said before you seemed like good skin - so why don't you lend a hand?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Fiadh conversation
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I'm getting glimpses of the future here and it's all death - not a tree or creature in sight. And none of my old tricks are shifting that.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Fiadh conversation
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: ...Ward...

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Fiadh conversation
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I don't follow?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Fiadh conversation
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Ward! Ha! Now that's a sign and a half!

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Fiadh conversation
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: A ward is a type of protection - I reckon the universe is telling me something.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Blake - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Then he goes and runs an event like this, and well - he's a very different man than he was a few years ago.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Blake - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you know the Marquess?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Blake - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Well... I thought I did. Not closely or personally, but as a figure, I reckoned I knew him.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Coventry
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: He's not the sort that you might see at an event like this, being that he has no interest in the occult or the 'scene' as the kids call it.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Coventry
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What do you make of Mister Coventry?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Coventry
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Grief can do strange things to a person. Not that I have seen much grieving in him; but then, we all process it in our own ways.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on O Finn
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Ah, he's a good laugh. We've known each other for a long time.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on O Finn
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: If you knew his druidic code of conduct, you'd know he and I are singing the same song, just... with different harmonies.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on O Finn
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you know Mister Ó Finn?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Mantovanni
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: She's a woman of many talents, to be sure. A shame she is so flippant in her use of them.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Mantovanni
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Still, I suppose it's hard to argue with the paycheck I hear she's been promised.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Mantovanni
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I would have expected a wise woman to be, well, wiser. Maybe all the bright lights have blinded her.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Mantovanni
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What do you think of Miss Mantovani?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Ah sure, what about me?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Why don't you tell me about yourself, Miss Callaghan?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Anything worth knowing is obvious to someone with a keen enough eye, Declan. You'll be fine.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Sorry, I am distracting you from something. I should leave you alone.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Ah, no Declan, I have the gift of "an dá shealladh". Just makes it hard to focus at times.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: But look, I'm talking the ears off you! You didn't come here to listen to me talking doom and gloom, eh?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: But this event... well, it does give me awful migraines to try and look at the future of it. And that is troublesome to me.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: And from that, I think you're alright, Declan!

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: An dá shealleadh? I've never heard of this...

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: It's a blessing and a curse that has allowed the women in my family insight into that which lies within and without.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: So you can see things that other people can't?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Do you jackeens learn nothing in that city of yours? The two sights, boy. It's something that's been with me since I can remember.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: It's more of an innate sense of the pattern, flow and weaving of Imbas about the place. But it does give me a good schniff of people.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Dupre
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I have. He's a good man - and one who acknowledges the intricate spirals of life, death and rebirth at that... But I fear he carries a shadow on his anam.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Dupre
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you spoken to Mister Dupré?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Dupre
speaker: Mister Ward

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Dupre
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: His soul, Declan. Lord almighty...

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Darcy
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Head in the sand, that one. Does not want to hear of the dangers of this place, only wants things she thinks readers will enjoy.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Darcy
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What do you make of Missus D'Arcy?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Darcy
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: No use gathering material for a book you may not live to write.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Father sinnot
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: What need do I have of a priest? I'm not dying?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Father sinnot
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you met Father Sinnott?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Father sinnot
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I'll say only this; some people are so caught up in a world that could be, that they're blind to the world they're already in.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Cathal
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Not sure I've ever been in the presence of angels before and I'm still not sure I have been...

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Cathal
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What impression do you have of Mister O'Meara?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Cathal
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: In need of a few slaps but there's a good lad in there somewhere - I have to wonder about his talk of angels, though.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Hazel
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: God help whoever she's set her sights on, I'd say she has a grip like a vice.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Hazel
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you met Missus Erickson?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Hazel
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Hazel Erickson? I wouldn't pay her any mind, she's a liar and a fake, through and through.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Ettiene
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: He's a pleasant man. I also think he has as much faith in our fellow guests as I do, though possibly for different reasons to myself.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Ettiene
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Good to have another sceptical set of eyes on the whole thing, even still. I think I might like to get to know him a bit better after all this is over.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Ettiene
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you spoken to Mister Toussaint?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Ettiene
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: ...if anything remains after, that is.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Arwa
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I don't know if its the pull of this place, or something buried away inside it, but she is not of her right mind.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Arwa
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What do you make of Miss Hisham?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Arwa
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: There's something wrong with that girl.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Arwa
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I see a black cloud around her head. Confusing her. A fog of the mind.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Arwa
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Whatever it is, she's liable to turn at any moment. Do not trust her lightly.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Ruairí
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Ah, my own flesh and blood! I've never had children myself, but Ruairí has been beside me like a shadow since he was small.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Ruairí
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What can you tell me about Doctor Callaghan?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Ruairí
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I've been training him up. Any day now, he'll be ready to take my place.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Ines
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Identity is a complex thing. She walks the line where her soul yearns for something her head can't fathom.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Ines
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What do you make of Miss Barbosa?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Ines
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Ah, she's got her troubles, but she's got a good head on her shoulders, too.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Ines
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: She'll do right in whatever she sets her mind to, I'm sure of that.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Saoirse
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you met Miss Murphy?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Saoirse
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Awww Declan. My poor heart.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Saoirse
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Our society is broken in so many ways, and it has failed this young woman in all of them.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Saoirse
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: If I could do something for the poor thing, I would.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Ivy
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I like her. Genuine and down to earth. Very few airs and graces for her background.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Ivy
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Nice to see a young woman in comfortable shoes.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Ivy
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What's your opinion on Miss McLeod?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Ivy
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Well, let me tell you this. My dhá sheallach isn't being affected by being in this place.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Ivy
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: And I saw nothing about her that would suggest the cause of her loss - all of which tells me it's not mystical in nature.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Ivy
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Whatever is happening to that girl, it's as un-magical as you or... well, you.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Ivy
speaker: Mister Ward

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Varley
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: The man needs to loosen up a bit! I've never seen anyone so dour in all my life.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Varley
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What do you make of Mister Varley?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Varley
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I do see him about Gauford, doing jobs from time to time.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Varley
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: You'd almost get the feeling that he's more against this séance than myself.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Lan Fen
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you met Missus Lau?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Lan Fen
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: She's a sharp one, isn't she? Fierce bad luck to be a widow at that age, but these things happen...

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Lan Fen
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: At least she's got Miss McLeod to take her to all sorts of interesting places.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Skerritt
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Oh Lord, have mercy on anyone cursed enough to have to deal with this small-minded amadán.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Skerritt
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you met Mister Skerritt?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Skerritt
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: He has strong opinions for a man who's achieved so little in his life. Achieved so little with so much, I might add.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Skerritt
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: If you or I had been born with a spoon so silver in our mouths, we might have changed the world.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Skerritt
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Instead, he decided to shove it up his thóin and do nothing.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Corentine
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Miss Quinn? I wasn't expecting her to have her feet on the ground like she does, I'll give her that.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What impression do you have of Miss Quinn?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Corentine
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Maybe it's that heaviness she's carrying; there's something on her shoulders much greater than any one person should have to bear.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Caitlin
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you happen to know Missus Joyce?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Caitlin
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Ah, Caitlin. I know her. She knows everyone's business, but that's nothing new - she's been a nosy beggar since we were small.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Caitlin
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Pious as anything, except for when she'd get caught - then she'd find somebody to sacrifice to save herself.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Darragh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I made it my business to get to know all the staff. Best source of information in a place like this. Better company, too.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Darragh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you happen to know Mister Hunter?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Darragh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Mister Hutner is a fine, strong gentleman - though I can't say I've noticed... ahem!

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Seamus
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Bit of a blank slate there, like he's blocked something out. Poor dear could do with a hug.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Seamus
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What do you make of Mister Doyle?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Deane
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you met Miss Deane?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Deane
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Pfft, I have.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Deane
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: You stay away from that one, Declan.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Deane
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Lest she try take what's of value to you.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Walter Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you know young Walter Blake?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Character Presents - Fiadh/Opinion on Walter Blake
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Well, I've heard of him. Everyone local has. Had hoped I'd get a good look at him while I was here, but he really does stick to the shadows, doesn't he?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Analysis Presents - (to) Fiadh/Unusual Hair Colour - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Might I ask how you came to have the white streak in your hair? I don't think I've seen its like, before.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Analysis Presents - (to) Fiadh/Unusual Hair Colour - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I've had it all my life. You should have seen me with it when I was a little girl!

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Analysis Presents - (to) Fiadh/Unusual Hair Colour - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Some people believe it's a sign of wisdom to be born with such a thing, you know.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Analysis Presents - (to) Fiadh/Unusual Hair Colour - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Now, I can't say for certain that that's true - but I do like the idea.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Analysis Presents - (to) Fiadh/Celtic Cross Necklace - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: That's a fine cross you have there.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Analysis Presents - (to) Fiadh/Celtic Cross Necklace - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Ah, this? This is just to keep the priests off my back. Between you and me, Declan, I don't much care for these new gods. Up on high on golden thrones? Pah!

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Analysis Presents - (to) Fiadh/Celtic Cross Necklace - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I prefer the old Gods, walking and working the land, side by side with us.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Analysis Presents - (to) Fiadh/Folk Jewellery - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I don't believe I've seen jewellery of the sort you're wearing before.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Analysis Presents - (to) Fiadh/Folk Jewellery - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Ah, well, a lot of it is handmade. Some of it brings me luck, and some of it protects me. They're old crafts, to be sure, but not soon forgotten.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Analysis Presents - (to) Fiadh/patches - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I see you are handy with a needle and thread.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Analysis Presents - (to) Fiadh/patches - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I can stitch up jumpers and wounds. All part of the work. No need throwing something out, when all it needs is a mend.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Resolution - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Oh gods, no. The séance is still going ahead - damage will still happen.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Resolution - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Satisfied?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Resolution - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: But we've protected the well.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Resolution - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: And...

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Resolution - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: ...I think a rift between Ruairí and I is mended.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Resolution - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Ah Declan. I'm so proud of him.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Resolution - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: What a fool I was to be such a stick in the mud!

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Resolution - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I should have trusted his new ways, and in doing so had faith in myself as a teacher.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Resolution - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I guess one always worries they've not done enough to prepare their young 'uns.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Resolution - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: But you have to let them fly, I suppose. And Ruairí? He soared.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Resolution - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Resolution - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Someday, Declan, by the grace of God, you'll have kids of your own. Then you'll know.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Deane's leaving letter - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: It turns out Miss Deane left a letter excusing herself from the event.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Deane's leaving letter - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Then Miss Deane sounds like a smarter person than I first gave her credit for.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Second Sight - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What do you know about the second sight?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Second Sight - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Well, Declan, some people are born with an innate ability to sense beyond the mundane.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Second Sight - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: There exists a certain interconnection and weaving of the interlacing patterns of life in its many forms.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Second Sight - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I myself can sense in my bones where a person or event is aligned in this network.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Second Sight - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: For others, they can see ahead in the pattern, sometimes in the forms of visions, often in the form of dreams.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Second Sight - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: You mentioned an ability of yours, an dhá sheallach, is it the same thing?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Second Sight - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I am very glad I am not one of these people. It can hold a great weight and a constant sense of unease.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Bedroom skeleton key - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: It seems that my instinct is not quite as on point as I thought.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Bedroom skeleton key - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Explain yourself, Mister Ward.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Bedroom skeleton key - Fiadh
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ CONFIDE IN HER ]

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Bedroom skeleton key - Fiadh
speaker: Detective Ward

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Bedroom skeleton key - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I'll come clean with you. I am here investigating the disappearance of Evelyn Deane.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Bedroom skeleton key - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I found this key in the hallway, I was just looking for the porter to return it.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Bedroom skeleton key - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I... "borrowed" this key to help with my investigations.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Bedroom skeleton key - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: You did, did you? Then you might be hurrying along to get it back to its rightful owner, hadn't you?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Bedroom skeleton key - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Thank you, Declan, for not being another of the liars. I'll be keeping a close eye and I'm happy to know you will be too.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Statement, Mister Doyle - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Mister Doyle said he overheard Miss Deane arguing with someone on Tuesday.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Statement, Mister Doyle - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: It's a new moon, Declan, on the eve of Samhain. The veil is thinning, emotions are high... and something, I think, is afoot.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Dead End - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I took the trouble of seeing about where Miss Deane went when she left, and I've found that her trail seems to stop in the middle of the hedge maze.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Dead End - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: As the veil thins, more gateways will open that'll be hard to see if you don't know how to look.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Dead End - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: How would I look? It's as if she vanished into thin air.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Dead End - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: One does not simply vanish into thin air, Declan, but there are realms beyond the one we stand in.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Dead End - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: And more occupiers of the land than ourselves.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Dead End - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I would start by looking beyond what your eyes want you to see. Eyes cannot always be trusted.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Silks - Fiadh
speaker: Miss McLeod
en: Oh, how kind of you. I'll put it with my others.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Silks - Fiadh
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ OFFER SILKS ]

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Silks - Fiadh
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ KEEP SILKS ]

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Silks - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I'll hold onto this for now.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/timetable - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Well, I do think it's quite likely I'll be out in the maze for most of it.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/timetable - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: It seems I'll be in the maze most of the day again, Declan! I've offered a few scrying sessions at the old well.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/timetable - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: This old well may not show it, but it needs a great deal more care than it likes to let on.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/timetable - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I'm tending to the old well, you see. It needs a great deal more care than it likes to let on.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/timetable - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Between all that, my dear nephew and I have lunch plans at one.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/timetable - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I want to run through my talk with him which, incidentally, is in the drawing room at three.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/timetable - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: After that, it's dinner at seven, and then feet up for the night!

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/timetable - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Otherwise, I still have lunch at one. And I'm seeing the drawing room talks at three and five.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/timetable - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Then, of course, it's time to face that damnable séance and see what's to come of it.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/timetable - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you have any plans for the weekend?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/timetable - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you have any plans for today?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/timetable - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Though my Ruairí does like to gab, so I'm sure we'll be in the dining room right up until my talk!

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/timetable - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: It would be lovely to see you there, Declan. We're doing it in the drawing room at three.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/timetable - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: As for tomorrow...

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/timetable - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: After all that, I think this evening calls for a few quiet hours in the library!

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/timetable - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: At least... now I feel watched over - safe. Ready for whatever is to come.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Bridge game - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Were you at the bridge game on Tuesday?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Bridge game - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I was, dear, and a fine thrashing we gave the posh beggers too, ha!

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Bridge game - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Oh, well, it was myself and little Ruairí against Marquess Blake and Mister Coventry - much to their dismay.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Bridge game - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Who was playing?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Bridge game - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: The other table was Miss Quinn and Missus Lau against Missus D'Arcy and poor Miss Barbosa, who thought it would be fun to play, but was soon set right in those thoughts.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Newspaper clipping - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: It seems like Missus Joyce has an interest in the goings on in Dublin.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Newspaper clipping - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Well, Declan... It seems, does it not, that the proverbial cat may be out of the bag?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Newspaper clipping - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: But look, I'll never judge a man for doing his job.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Drafted telegram - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: It appears Missus Joyce sent for help - that she was worried about Miss Deane.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Drafted telegram - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Well if anyone would know, it would be Caitlin.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Drafted telegram - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: And if she is concerned enough to telegram... then that in itself is concerning enough to me.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Entertainment schedule - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: A caught a glimpse of the entertainment schedule for the week... they are packing quite a lot in!

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Entertainment schedule - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Orchestrated to divert, Declan. Don't be fooled.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Entertainment schedule - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Even the magpie knows when to be cautious of novel, flashy distractions.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Entertainment schedule - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Though I confess even I fell a little. A few games of bridge on Tuesday night but I forgive myself. Guilt is for the  Catholics.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/cigar burns - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Mister Skerritt, conveniently for him, fell asleep in one with a lit cigar - just as we were supposed to play a game of bridge. But then, that did give me cause to send for my Ruairí.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/cigar burns - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: We played a lot when he was little. He doesn't like to let on, but he's quite good - and a better partner than that old man would have been.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/cigar burns - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Who'd be smoking in the library armchairs?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/talks - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I can't say I was expecting there to be talks at this event.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/talks - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: It's for the better, I say. These people ought to learn something about what they're doing while they're here.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/talks - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Maybe they might even think better of it.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Memento Mori - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you happen to know anything about the Quinn family having an unusual number of deaths?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Memento Mori - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Ah. Quite a story, that one. And not a happy one. Now, it was before my time that the Quinns were still in Ireland...

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Memento Mori - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: But as I hear it, they moved to England to try and escape a curse put upon them. I hear it didn't work.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Memento Mori - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: ... And so the Quinns are still cursed to reach untimely ends, every one of them. There can't be many left, now. Miss Quinn might be one of the last.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Hiring telegram - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What do you make of this?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Hiring telegram - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I wish I could say I'm surprised that there's something not right afoot here... but I'd be lying.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Hiring telegram - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I do hope you find that girl. She might be a fool, but she doesn't deserve harm to come to her.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Photograph of Deane - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you recognise this woman?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Photograph of Deane - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Oh, yes. Miss Deane, isn't it? She's been about.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/The Grand Séance - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you been to an event such as this one before?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/The Grand Séance - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Such as this one, with a rake of so-called magicians looking to tamper with the very fabric of our world?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/The Grand Séance - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: No, I haven't been that unlucky. Looks like my luck's run out, eh?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/The Grand Séance - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I couldn't think of a worse use for all this know-how if I tried.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/The Grand Séance - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Mark my words - this little trick of theirs, if it works, will be devastating.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/The Grand Séance - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Mark my words - I might be here to watch from a distance, but that's exactly what I'll do. I'll have nothing to do with that séance.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/The Grand Séance - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I've seen it on the wind and I feel it in my bones.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Marriage talk - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I've heard talk there's a young lady hoping to find a suitable marriage candidate here.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Marriage talk - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Here? Oh, God bless her!

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Marriage talk - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Whatever has the world come to?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Blake Family - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you know much about the Blake family?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Blake Family - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Can't say I've ever felt the need to give them any time, thinking about them or otherwise.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Blake Family - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: The Blakes have taken enough from this place and the people here.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Blake Manor - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you know anything about the manor?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Blake Manor - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: They say it was built by the first Blake to come to Ireland - that he was given the land by Cromwell himself.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Blake Manor - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: It wasn't their land to give or receive - but that didn't stop them, now, did it?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Edward Blake - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What do you know about Edward Blake?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Edward Blake - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: He was a high-ranking officer in Cromwell's crusade. I don't recall the exact details.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Edward Blake - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: What I do know is that he was a scourge on this place, before and after he was awarded the land.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Edward Blake - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: The worst sort of man; the kind that could put devils to shame.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Well scrying - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I've heard that you have been known to offer people well scrying. What is that, exactly?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Well scrying - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Well, to put it simply, scrying means looking. Looking for answers, or to somewhere you couldn't otherwise see.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Well scrying - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: And wells have a lot of power about them, you know. If you ask a question to one, it might give you answers.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Well scrying - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: If you're lucky, it'll even show you what you're looking for.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Well scrying - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: That's what I do - I ask the well for answers or information. More often than not, it more than provides.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Photo of child - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you think you'd be able to lead Miss Murphy in well scrying?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Photo of child - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: It would do her good to see her daughter, but the Magdalene Laundry that took her child - they won't share any information.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Photo of child - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I can think of no better cause. You tell Miss Murphy I'm ready whenever she is, and to meet me at the well.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Hauntings - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I've heard tell that this manor is haunted... Have you seen anything of the sort?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Hauntings - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: There's more spirits here than any one place should have, Declan, I can tell you that.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Hauntings - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: A generosity of ghosts these past two hundred and fifty years.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Hauntings - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Started with the bloody wound Cromwell cut into this land...

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Hauntings - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: ...and carried on through generations of Edward Blake's depraved descendants.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Ritual Markings - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I found evidence of a ritual being performed upstairs.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Ritual Markings - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Did you now? No one has mentioned anything of the sort to me.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Ritual Markings - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: That means it's some exclusive, high society nonsense, or it's something the person performing it doesn't want anyone else to know about. Hmm...

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Letter to Sister in Law - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Doctor Callaghan's mother must be proud of him following your footsteps?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Letter to Sister in Law - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Ha! Oh yes, she's thrilled her doctor son is committed to a life of helping the poor, instead of earning himself a fine income.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Letter to Sister in Law - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Given the chance, the woman would burn me for a witch, only for my brother who stills her hand.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Séance Purpose - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What do you make of the intent of this séance?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Séance Purpose - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I couldn't think of a worse use for all this know-how if I tried.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Séance Purpose - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Mark my words - I might be here to watch from a distance, but that's exactly what I'll do. I'll have nothing to do with that séance.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Hedonistic Gala - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Did you enjoy the masked ball, Miss Callaghan?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Hedonistic Gala - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Didn't go. I wasn't about to head to a thing like that. I was playing cards with the staff for most of it.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Hedonistic Gala - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: The costumes were something else, though! I'll give you all that.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Strange Dreams - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I have found my dreams quite disturbed since coming here.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Strange Dreams - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: That doesn't surprise me in the least - there's foul play afoot here with this séance business.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Strange Dreams - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: People dreaming they're wandering the halls, trying to get out of this place, then end up at the séance instead.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Strange Dreams - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: And still they want to attend the damn thing? What more warning could they want that it's a bad idea!

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Sketches of Strange Symbol - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I've been seeing a sketch of a symbol around I don't recognise. Here, I made a copy. Does this mean anything to you?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Sketches of Strange Symbol - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: That's curious... I don't think I've seen it before. Whatever could that mean?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Fetters - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I've been told that a ghost requires "fetters" to keep it attached to this world. Would that be right?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Fetters - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: That's about the right of it.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Fetters - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: There has to be something to keep them here. Usually it's some emotional tie.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Fetters - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: If a person dies wishing they could have finished some affair of theirs, or with a lot of anger, they're much more likely to return as a spirit.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Ms Callaghan's Perspective - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: If I might ask, Miss Callaghan... Am I right in thinking you're... less than satisfied with the course Doctor Callaghan is taking?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Ms Callaghan's Perspective - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: He should know better than to get involved with all this high society magic nonsense, Declan. I taught him better than that.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Ms Callaghan's Perspective - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Our craft isn't about social climbing or fancy parties, it's about respect and balance.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Ms Callaghan's Perspective - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I think he's losing sight of that for what it can gain him, instead.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Dr Callaghan's Perspective - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I have the impression that perhaps Doctor Callaghan has taken to this sort of high-society event because he doesn't feel respected as things are.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Dr Callaghan's Perspective - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: What makes you say that?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Dr Callaghan's Perspective - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: He's an accomplished practitioner, isn't he?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Dr Callaghan's Perspective - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: He's one of the best.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Dr Callaghan's Perspective - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: And yet you still consider him your apprentice. Perhaps he finds that demeaning?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Dr Callaghan's Perspective - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: But I don't mean it like that! I...

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Dr Callaghan's Perspective - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Perhaps I should talk to him.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Unknown Sigil - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I've been seeing this sigil about the place. A spiral with four lines intersecting it. Have you seen anything of its type?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Unknown Sigil - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I don't believe I have, but I'll be sure to look out for it.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Curse - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I have heard that Miss Quinn's family are under some sort of curse?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Curse - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Ah, so she's one of those Quinns - it all makes sense, now. That's a lot of tragedy for one family... but they did visit it upon themselves, at least in the beginning.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Curse - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: She seems like a nice girl herself, though. I hope it doesn't get her - we could do with more people like her around.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Deane's Room - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you know which room Miss Deane was staying in?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Deane's Room - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Now, Declan, I might be nosy, but I'm not quite that nosy. Your guess would be as good as mine.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Deane's Room - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: She couldn't be near me anyway, I've not seen her in days.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Skull mask - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: You weren't wearing a skull mask to the ball last night, were you?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Skull mask - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: To the - ? My dear Declan, I wasn't at the ball. You wouldn't catch me dead at a thing like that.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Skull mask - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: No offence meant, of course.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Red hair - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I found a red hair inside a fallen mask. Does that mean anything to you?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Red hair - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Well, it's not mine, if that's what you're asking. I wasn't at the ball.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Well Symbols - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I noticed that the well has been covered in these strange symbols. Would you have any idea what they mean?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Well Symbols - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I should certainly hope so! I'm the one who drew them.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Well Symbols - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Oh, the land here has suffered, Declan. I fear this séance, and all its agendas, may push her past the edge.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Well Symbols - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: But I fear all these short-sighted people have left us more in need of an optician than a healer.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Well Symbols - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: That well is a pillar of the land - has been since the time of the gods. If it is safe, the land will be safe.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Well Symbols - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: The symbols are simply protective.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Miss Callaghan's Components - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Have you had any luck?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Miss Callaghan's Components - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Not yet...

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Miss Callaghan's Components - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Well, I have faith in you. An dhá sheallach has me believing this is the right course of action, however unorthodox it might seem. Godspeed, Declan.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Strange Occurences - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Ah Declan, you can't actually be asking me that. Sure, the whole place is mad!

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Strange Occurences - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you noticed anything strange since coming here?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Strange Occurences - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Whispers in walls, laughter outside the windows, and no heat from the fire.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Strange Occurences - Fiadh
