speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: It's wall to wall strangeness.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Notes on Milesian Blood Magic - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Did you know that Miss Deane hails from a powerful Milesian bloodline? That's what I've been hearing, at least.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Notes on Milesian Blood Magic - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Does she now? That little... no wonder she...

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Notes on Milesian Blood Magic - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: ...Oh, I've no time to spend on bitterness, Declan.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Notes on Milesian Blood Magic - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I'll hope she miraculously puts it to good use, and leave it at that.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Coded Papers - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Does this ring any bells for you, Miss Callaghan?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Coded Papers - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: What an intricate sigil...

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Coded Papers - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: It seems to suggest something hidden, Declan. And perhaps something that would best remain so.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Magical Grimoire - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Are you familiar with this book, Miss Callaghan?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Magical Grimoire - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: ...I am not. And I absolutely don't want to be.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Magical Grimoire - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Whatever those sigils open or close, I want no part in it.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Magical Grimoire - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Is that what they say?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Magical Grimoire - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: ...Yes. One opens and the other closes. What - I cannot say, but it's old, powerful, and not for trifling with.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Witchcraft components - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What do you make of these? They look like components for a spell or charm of some kind to me.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Witchcraft components - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: For a charm indeed, Declan. But for good or ill, I couldn't say. Either way, simple magic can be very powerful in the right hands.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Chimney Charm - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I found this on the grounds. What do you make of it?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Chimney Charm - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Well, look at that. I'd imagine you found it in a chimney or under some floorboards? Why you're poking around hard-to-reach hiding places is your own business, Declan.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Chimney Charm - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: It's a simple charm, needs to be close to the person it's targeting. Looks like it's meant to bind a magic user - stop them from moving or hurting another person, that sort of thing.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Mister Callaghan's Components - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I was speaking to Doctor Callaghan, and he seems to think these could aid your attempts to heal the well.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Mister Callaghan's Components - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Oh, Ruairí. How many times do I have to tell you?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Mister Callaghan's Components - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: You can try these modern methods all you like, but they'll never be as robust or as studied as the old ways.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Mister Callaghan's Components - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Quick fixes always come back to bite you, Declan. Remember that.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Bean Draoi - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: You mentioned you were a Bean Draoí? What's that, now?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Bean Draoi - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Ah, it's like a hedge witch. I offer treatments, both physical and spiritual, to the locals.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Bean Draoi - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: And I look after the land too. Really, though, a land and its people are intertwined, so it's all one.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Bean Draoi duties - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Can you tell me more of your duties?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Bean Draoi duties - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Oh, em... What else is there to say? Healing of the land, the body, the mind - all that.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Bean Draoi duties - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Some veterinary work. Blessings on the land and tributes to keep the Other Folk happy. I do the odd bit of scrying for those with the need for it.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Bean Draoi duties - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: And I train successors. Or, at least I try. Ruairí's been on and off that path, these days...

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/seance aftermath - faidh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Why do you think the séance is so dangerous?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/seance aftermath - faidh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Declan. Are you a holy man?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/seance aftermath - faidh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I am.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/seance aftermath - faidh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Then you'd be of the mind that all this, how all this works, is God's will - God's design, yes?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/seance aftermath - faidh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I suppose that would be fair.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/seance aftermath - faidh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Whatever system you live by has starts and ends. To pull that apart - with no plan to patch it up, mind, is to open a door that was never meant to be opened.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/seance aftermath - faidh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: It's what the Greeks called a Pandora's Box.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Mary Blake - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What can you tell me about Marchioness Blake?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Mary Blake - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Mary? I can tell you she didn't care much for that title.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Mary Blake - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: We only spoke a few times. She had trouble conceiving, so she came to me under the dead of night for some alternative help.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Mary Blake - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: The Marquess wouldn't have liked that sort of thing, then. Funny how death changes us.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Mary Blake - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I never heard much of how it turned out, but the boy's on the walls, so it must have worked.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Mary Blake - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: ...Not that I doubted it would, mind you!

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Goibniu - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What do you know about the name Goibniu?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Goibniu - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: A smithing god, same as Bríd. My understanding is his work focused more on war - weapons and armour, you see, whereas her work was more for daily tasks - horseshoes, tools, pots, and the likes.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/fae - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What can you tell me about the fae?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/fae - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: The Other Folk, you mean? I'd be careful - especially here, now. As we near Samhain, the veil gets thinner and thinner - it's not only ghosts that draw near.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Tuatha Dé Danann - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Can you tell me about the Tuatha Dé Danann?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Tuatha Dé Danann - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: The old gods. They are all around us. In the hills, the rivers, the valleys.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Tuatha Dé Danann - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I like that. I like when I am angry with a god, I can go to their house and yell at them.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Tuatha Dé Danann - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Just below the surface, where the other place can sometimes be found.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Brid - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Can you tell me about the goddess Bríd?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Brid - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Well. As the Cailleach is the winter, they say Bríd is the summer. One of the fairest and most loved goddesses.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Brid - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: It's said that when her son was killed by Goibniu that she keened the first keening. All other keening since, is her sharing that sorrow with mortalkind and knowing their pain of loss.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/morrigan - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Can you speak on the Morrigan?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/morrigan - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: And what could I tell you? That's she's a blood-hungry madwoman? Or that she's the great saviour of this land? A mother of monsters and lover of mankind?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/morrigan - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Maybe she's all of it, maybe she's not, maybe she's that and more. I don't truly know. I don't walk her path, and I've not met her.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/morrigan - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: The monks who wrote down our ways edited our ways. So, is she the villain they made her out to be? Maybe, but I'd wager she was more likely just a powerful and headstrong lass. That's villain enough for those monastic boys.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Cailleach - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Can you tell me anything about the Cailleach?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Cailleach - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I've sat on her chair at the spring equinox to welcome the days and then again on the autumn one to bid them farewell.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Cailleach - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I've crawled through her house on  Slieve Gullion and caught a glimpse of the Otherworld.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Cailleach - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: In return she sometimes visits me in my sleep and teaches me a trick or two. It's from her I have my dhá sheallach.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Cailleach - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: A bit, aye. It's her I welcome in when I form the circle and make space for intentions to form.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/tir na nog - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What can you tell me about Tír na nÓg?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/tir na nog - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: It's the home of the Gods, Declan. And not just the Gods - the Fair Folk, and our dead too.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/tir na nog - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: It's sort of underneath us, and it isn't - as is the way of such places.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/tir na nog - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Caverns like Oweynagat, or cairns of important people, or dolmens.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/tir na nog - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Significant ways under, down and through.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/tir na nog - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: But it's there enough that coming and going is possible through passageways, found at places of great power, once the day is dark.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/tir na nog - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Significant ways under and down and through.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Well - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you know anything about the hedge maze's well?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Well - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I know everything about it! Do you know that the gods themselves would have drunk water from that well?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Well - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: It's been imbued with their power. As long as that water is pure, the land around it will prosper.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Milesians - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What can you tell me about Milesians?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Milesians - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Well, that's the race of man who came to this island and battled the gods for the right to stay.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Milesians - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Funny - we first fought them, then we worshipped them. Then we, largely, forgot.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Milesians - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I like that more than worshipping the God that we all lost to in the end, myself.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Milesians - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Ruairí is talking more about this at 3pm tomorrow, you know. You could do worse than go to that for more.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Milesians - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Ruairí is talking more about this at 3pm today, you know. You could do worse than go to that for more.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Milesians - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Ruairí was talking about today, you know. You could do worse than ask him about this.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Letter from Dr Callaghan - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: It seems Doctor Callaghan has been in recent correspondence with Miss Deane.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Letter from Dr Callaghan - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: That wee scrut! I told him to stay away from her! Writing to her behind my back, no less!

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Letter from Dr Callaghan - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: She'd be the ruin of him!

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Letter from Dr Callaghan - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: And you mark my words, I won't let that happen...

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/aunt's shadow - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you think it's hard for Ruairí being your apprentice for all these years?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/aunt's shadow - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Even now, I worry that little shadow could disappear entirely inside my own.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/aunt's shadow - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: That'll get you in just as much trouble as never stopping to think in the first place.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/aunt's shadow - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: It's been a long road, yes. He's been in my shadow since he was small.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/aunt's shadow - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: But, he can still be a bit in his own head. Tries to think his way through when he should be feeling instead.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/aunt's shadow - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: He'll get there. He's just not there yet.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/rejected request - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Is it true that Miss Deane asked you to teach her Irish magic?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/rejected request - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: The nerve of her. She didn't ask, she demanded.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/rejected request - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: A means, not an end. It wasn't the path for her.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/rejected request - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Not much gets by you, does it Declan?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/rejected request - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: For her attitude alone I'd reject her, but you can't just learn these things on a course. It's a way of life.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/protector - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: How do you protect something like the well and the water?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/protector - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Normally my work is less abstract. A sick lamb or a boy who needs the cure of a bad cough.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/protector - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Right?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/protector - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Declan, between you, me, and the breeze, I'm still figuring that bit out on the job.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/protector - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: But the gods wouldn't give me a task I wasn't able for.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/gauge - fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What do you make of that strange device in the atrium?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/gauge - fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: That worrisome jar of green energy? I've seen it. I've poked it. I've even spilled wine on it, but nothing seems to deter it from whatever it is doing.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/gauge - fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I have a bad feeling about it, Declan.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/washer woman - fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Ah Declan. I'm sorry for whatever loss you've suffered.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/washer woman - fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: When I arrived, I thought I saw a woman washing clothes in the fountain.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/washer woman - fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: The bean nigh, she's called. An omen of death to come. This is the kind of thing I was warning people about.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/washer woman - fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: If you're seeing her, we'll have death before this weekend is over. If it hasn't already happened.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/washer woman - fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: The bean nigh, she's only clearly visible to those who're grieving. She's lured by the death to come, but can be seen by those with death's touch still on them - those still grieving for love lost.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/washer woman - fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Why did you say sorry for my loss?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Shadowy Figure - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Can you think of anything that might explain a large, ghostly figure on the land?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Shadowy Figure - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: All this messing has lured some of the Fair Folk here. Or maybe awoken one of the Tuatha? ...Ah, don't look at me like a feckless cow, Declan. The Tuatha Dé Danann!

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Shadowy Figure - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Ah, now they've gone and done it! I warned them that nothing good would come of this séance. It's not a ghost, that's for sure - they only come in the one size...

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Evidence Presents - Fiadh/Shadowy Figure - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: The old Gods! Gone from our plain to the Otherworld, but sure, what kind of god can't walk among its people every now and then?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Fiadh not missing
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Miss Callaghan is present and accounted for. The red hair wasn't hers.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Fiadh not missing
speaker: Mister Ward
en: There's only one other person here with hair that colour and length...

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Fiadh not missing
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Domhnall Ó Finn must be our missing man.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Ward in room - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Declan Ward, what on this dying Earth is wrong with you?

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Ward in room - Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Fiadh-

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Ward in room - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: That's Miss Callaghan to you! Breaking and entering, what-

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Ward in room - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Come with me. Mister Varley is going to have words for you, I promise you that.

conversation: Cast/Fiadh Callaghan/Ward in room - Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Sir, what on this dying earth is wrong with you?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/JBlake conversation
speaker: Detective Ward
en: LEAVE

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/JBlake conversation
speaker: Mister Ward
en: If you'll excuse me, Marquess Blake.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/JBlake conversation
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Ah. Mister Ward. How can I help?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/JBlake conversation
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Ah, a new guest. You would be Mister Ward, then?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/JBlake conversation
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I am the Marquess of Doon, Jonathan Blake. A pleasure.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/JBlake conversation
speaker: Mister Ward
en: You have the better of me, Sir.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/JBlake conversation
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Well then, Mister Ward. Welcome to my home and to the Grand Séance. I hope, whatever you are looking for, you find it here.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/JBlake conversation
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: No, not really - I know nothing more than your name. That is why I invited you to lunch today, to meet you before the séance later.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/JBlake conversation
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I do hope you will attend.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/JBlake conversation
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: A shame you did not attend.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/JBlake conversation
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I seem to have missed that invite, Marquess. But now that I'm aware of it, I will do my best to be there.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/JBlake conversation
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Thank you for the invite, Marquess. I certainly hope to see you there.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/JBlake conversation
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I seem to have missed that invite, Marquess. My apologies for not attending.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/JBlake conversation
speaker: Mister Ward
en: My apologies for not attending. There is so much to see around the manor that the - well the morning, it just got away from me.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/JBlake conversation
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: No real harm done, Mister Ward. Welcome to my home and to the Grand Séance. I hope, whatever you are looking for, you find it here.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/JBlake conversation
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Of course.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/catches ward in residence
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Mister Ward! What on earth are you doing in here?!

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/catches ward in residence
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Guests are not permitted in the private wing. As well you know.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/catches ward in residence
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: You may take your bags and leave, Sir.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/bridge game
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you know who attended?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/bridge game
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Were you at the bridge game on Tuesday?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/bridge game
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Yes. I have been trying to spend time with all the event participants. It was a suitable way to meet many at once.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/bridge game
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Honestly, not all of them. Miss Callaghan organised it, I believe. Her and her boy - the doctor - were there. Simon... Mister Coventry, too. And... the second table... I cannot recall.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/talks - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: The guests seem convinced this place is... haunted... Perhaps, if ghosts are the memory of a place, they are right.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/talks - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Certainly, she is an old building with lots of history. I thought perhaps sharing some of that might add... perspective to their... hunt.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/The Grand Séance - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: A séance is a strange event to host. How did that come to be?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/The Grand Séance - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: It was the abruptness with which she was taken. So much left unsaid.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/The Grand Séance - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I... lost my wife a few years ago. A carriage accident. It was... a difficult time for me.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/The Grand Séance - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I found some comfort through visiting a medium.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/The Grand Séance - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I would not say it "healed" me, but it helped me get on this path.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/The Grand Séance - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Naturally, I became interested in the practice and wanted to do my part in forwarding the field.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/The Grand Séance - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I have no abilities there, so to speak, but I have this manor - and so that is what I offer up.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Hotel Finances - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: An event like this must be a real boost for the hotel's income?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Hotel Finances - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: One hopes. But this is about more than profit, Mister Ward - money unrecovered is still money well spent.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Mary Blake - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I heard of your late wife. My condolences.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Mary Blake - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: My thanks, Mister Ward.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Mary Blake - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: You know, it was a controversial marriage. Her family were not of high enough status for my title.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Mary Blake - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: My Aunt Catherine, God rest her soul, was just glad I had married at all. She felt I had thrown too much of myself into this hotel business.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Mary Blake - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: She was right, of course. After the hardships of the famines, I had felt it was important to secure the family house and finances.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Mary Blake - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: But then, if Mary had not come to stay here, we would never have met - and so the great wheel turns.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Mary Blake - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Have you ever felt love, Mister Ward? She unlocked me, is how I would describe it.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Mary Blake - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: She was, is, my everythi--

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Mary Blake - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: ...I ...am sorry, Mister Ward. You will have to excuse me a moment.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Mary Blake - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: But for whom, with no heirs?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Mary Blake - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Hedonistic Gala - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: If you will forgive my forwardness, but I was not expecting a gala quite like the one of last night.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Hedonistic Gala - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I assure you, Mister Ward, neither was I. But these things - rituals, I mean - have, well... rituals.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Hedonistic Gala - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: You mean to say that was part of the séance?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Hedonistic Gala - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Part of the preparation for it, yes. Tonight we perform the séance, but we have been hurtling towards it for some time now.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Hedonistic Gala - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: With the ball, we crossed one of the final thresholds, the point of no return.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Strange Dreams - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Might I ask - is there a history of people having strange dreams in the manor?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Strange Dreams - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I only dream of my wife and son, Mister Ward. There is nothing strange about that.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Strange Dreams - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: As for what my ancestors dreamt, I could not say.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Hauntings - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: It is likely the time of year and the event playing with my mind, but I could swear I have seen... things. Figures in the distance.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Hauntings - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: There have been reports of hauntings on the manor and its grounds as far back as my family has held it.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Hauntings - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Certainly, I have encountered the occasional oddity, myself.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Hauntings - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: What do I think they are? In truth, I do not know. Are they even real? Well... on that, all I can say is the Blake family records are littered with mysterious deaths and insanities that have no other explanation...

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Hauntings - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Hopefully tonight, we will find out for certain.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Deane's Room - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you know which room Miss Deane was staying in?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Deane's Room - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: No. If, for some reason, you must know, you might ask the manager. I'm not concerned with such things.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Deane's Invitation - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Did you personally invite Miss Deane to the manor, Marquess?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Deane's Invitation - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: The only guest that was invited was Miss Mantovani. Her name was enough to bring the rest.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Deane's Invitation - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: ...I did. A number of guests were invited. Then others, like yourself, just... showed up.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Deane's Invitation - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Miss Deane's late departure is frustrating enough without her having been invited, frankly.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/map of the region - blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Might I ask how much of this area belongs to you and your family?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/map of the region - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I'm unsure any more. We owned quite a lot a long time ago. Some have been sold over the years, or traded as dowries.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/map of the region - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: There are records, but I'd have to go and search them.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/blake manor - blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Has the manor been open to the public for long?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/blake manor - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I took over the titles and lands when my father died in the mid 1860s.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/blake manor - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: The manor was over two hundred years old by then, and needed much work.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/blake manor - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: But the famine did not leave a lot of spare funds, so I opened the place as a hotel to help finance the renovations. This was in the spring of 1870.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/blake manor - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: The work is never-ending, so we stay open. But it wasn't for that reason alone - it's nice to have people here. When I was young, there were more of us.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/blake manor - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: And, I'm told, in my grandfather's time and before that, there were many families under the roof.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/blake manor - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: It was not made to sit here idle. It is good for the house to have life in it.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/seance contract - blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Might I ask how you secured Miss Mantovani's talents? It is a long way to go for work, no?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/seance contract - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: To be frank, Mister Ward, she was secured the way all talent is - money.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/seance contract - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: But it is an investment I stand behind, both financially and spiritually.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/vase - blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Does the vase in these drawings look familiar?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/vase - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I have seen it before. I think perhaps in a family portrait?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/catacombs - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Does the manor have catacombs or other underground passages?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/catacombs - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Almost certainly, Mister Ward. The estate has a long and storied history.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/catacombs - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I know of some half-collapsed corridors and a closed-in bolthole, but I would not be surprised to learn of more.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/catacombs - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Who knows what secrets my ancestors held and what threats they needed to run from.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/catacombs - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: And, of course, the place was built atop an old settlement, which no doubt has its own secrets to add to the mix...

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/shadowy figure - blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have there ever been legends of giant creatures stalking the manor grounds?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/shadowy figure - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I've heard and read about many supernatural sightings here, but nothing like that. You could ask the staff, perhaps?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/timetable - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Are the silent dinner and séance not enough for you, Mister Ward? Certainly I expect they will keep me busy much of the day.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/timetable - blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Anything interesting planned for today?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/timetable - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I will make time for Mister Coventry's talk, however. It's always interesting to hear an outsider's perspective on one's home.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/recluse - blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Your son, Walter - he keeps to himself?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/recluse - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: He is not best suited to life in a hotel, but our private residence is large enough that he is never forced to face that reality.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/recluse - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Would he have been different, had the accident not happened? His mother was certainly more social than I. Perhaps he would have learned some of that from her.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/carraige accident - blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Might I ask, what actually caused the carriage accident?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/carraige accident - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: ...I suppose you might.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/carraige accident - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: It happened three years ago. Mary had taken the boy to Gauford for a treat, to see the boats. I suspect there was no reason for it, other than her good heart.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/carraige accident - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: A storm came in that day, quickly. The driver suggested they return to the manor before it became too severe.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/carraige accident - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: That this happened on October 31st is an irony not lost on me - though it is entirely coincidental.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/carraige accident - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: But they left it too late. The roads were muddy, the winds strong. A tree fell, and in his efforts to avoid it, the driver lost control of the carriage.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/carraige accident - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: It tumbled, and Mary was... well, she was gone.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/carraige accident - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: The driver succumbed to his own injuries a few hours later, bleeding out. No doctor could get here in time to save him.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/carraige accident - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: The driver, bless him, managed to pull Walter out and carried him back to the manor.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/crippled walter - blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: It must be difficult, your son's injuries.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/crippled walter - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I am not sure which is worse, Mary's death or his injuries.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/crippled walter - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: To know so much of his life has been taken from him. He'll never ride a horse, nor dance with the woman he loves.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/crippled walter - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Will he find love? Will it matter if he does? Or does the Blake line end with him.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/crippled walter - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I would give anything, do anything, take any risk to undo what has been done to him...

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/crippled walter - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: ...if that were an option...

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/crippled walter - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/end of line - blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Are there many Blakes left?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/end of line - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: No doubt, some distant relatives exist somewhere, but I don't know of them.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/end of line - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: No. The manor was full once, the family larger, but it is just Walter and I now.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/end of line - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: The numbers dwindle each generation - tragedy and marriage into other families.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/end of line - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: The west of Ireland is very remote - once a woman has been betrothed, she rarely keeps in touch - and is even less likely to return.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/refusal to remarry - blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I am told there is some scandal around your choice not to remarry?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/refusal to remarry - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Is there now? I did my duty, I married and sired. Perhaps it did not work out as intended, but I am under no further obligation.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/refusal to remarry - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I have not met another woman like Mary. Perhaps our vows were 'until death do us part', but I will face her at God's door as true to her as I ever was.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/fall from grace - blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: An event like this - it must seem strange to your peers?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/fall from grace - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Mister Ward... I have no peers.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/fall from grace - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: This is my land and my coin. I will make use of it in any way I wish.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/fall from grace - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Let the babbling masses complain. It only serves to highlight how little they understand. Or dare to understand.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Séance contract - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Forgive my discussion of money at a time like this, but... surely Miss Mantovani's talents couldn't have come cheap?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Séance contract - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: No, indeed. But for an event so important as this one, I will only have the best.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Séance contract - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: And this séance is very important?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Séance contract - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Mister Ward... Have you not figured that out by now? The expense, the people, the distance they have come...

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Séance contract - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: It will be one of the most important nights in history.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/wilhmena blake - Jblake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: But yes, I do recall that she disappeared. We have a portrait of her in the lobby, I believe. And, no doubt, something on her in the library, if you are interested.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/wilhmena blake - Jblake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Does the name Wilhelmina Blake mean anything to you?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/wilhmena blake - Jblake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Ah. A great-aunt of mine, if I am not mistaken. I don't recall much about her - she disappeared long before I arrived into the world.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Memento Mori - Etienne
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you happen to know about any... unusual rumours afflicting the Quinn family?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Memento Mori - Etienne
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: You're asking about the curse, of course.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Memento Mori - Etienne
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: The Quinns left Ireland before my time, but they still have many holdings here.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Memento Mori - Etienne
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Something happened there, and a curse was put on them. I'm told they moved to England to escape it, but to no avail.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/Memento Mori - Etienne
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: They are still cursed to reach untimely ends, every one of them. There are not many left. Miss Quinn is one of the last.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/fae - blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Can you tell me anything about the fae?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/fae - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I know the workers on the land leave out tribute to them and blame them when the crops go wrong.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/fae - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: When a person goes missing, it's often blamed on them too. Or, when a child has an accident...

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/gauge - blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What can you tell me about the strange device in the atrium?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/gauge - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: The gauge? It was built for this event - it is a measure of our collective psychic energy, a measure of how ready we are to pierce the veil.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/gauge - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: And thus a predictor of the séance's success.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/gauge - blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: It was full when I arrived, but that is no longer the case. Will that impact things?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/gauge - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I cannot say for certain, but a fuller reading would be preferable.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/gauge - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I'm sure Miss Mantovani will overcome any obstacles she encounters, however.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/washer woman - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I have seen this woman. Though she is no woman - she is a spectre. I see her across the manor. More now as the place fills and the hour draws near.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/washer woman - blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: When I arrived, I... I saw a woman washing something in the fountain.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/washer woman - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Sometimes I think she is Mary, but... No...

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/After Mary Blake - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Thank you. Now. Where were we?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/will - blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Did you know that Mister Coventry has left all of his earthly possessions to Walter in his will?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/will - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Has he? How... unusual. I suppose he has no children of his own... He must have taken a shine to the boy.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/will - blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Still...

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/cigar burn
speaker: Mister Ward
en: If you don't mind me asking, Marquess, do you happen to know what caused those burns on the library armchair?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Evidence Presents - Blake/cigar burn
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I hadn't noticed Mister Ward. I'll be sure to tell Mister Varley to have it seen to.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Ivy
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Miss McLeod? Ah, yes, the seer. Of course - how could I not make time?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Ivy
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you spoken to Miss McLeod at all?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Ivy
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I had hoped she'd be able to provide insights into our future success, but alas, she seems weakened.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Ivy
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I assume too many powerful minds in one place, but I could well be wrong.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Varley
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Has Mister Varley been with you long?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Varley
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Since the beginning. He's a fine man, a loyal man. I know this event does not sit well with him and the other staff, but they understand it's important to me, and so they work their damndest to make it work. That's the attitude one needs in servants.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Lan Fen
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Missus Lau. The Chinese lady, I presume?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Lan Fen
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you know Missus Lau?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Lan Fen
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: She was at a bridge game I attended last week. A keen player.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Lan Fen
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: She is more interested in what is taking place here than she admits. Why the pretence, I do not know.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Skerritt
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you met Mister Skerritt?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Skerritt
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: The banker, yes. For a man who has never experienced love he has a lot of opinions on what it might be.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Skerritt
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I suspect it was his attention that drove Miss Deane off, in the end.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you met Miss Quinn before?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Corentine
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Before this event, no. But I have family who know - or rather, knew - hers. She and I have spoken during her stay. Miss Quinn seems well-versed in her esoteric studies, and I'm glad to have her here.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Caitlin
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Missus Joyce is your housekeeper, yes?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Caitlin
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: The housekeeper, yes - though not just that. Since my wife's passing, Missus Joyce has carried the burden of being Walter's caretaker.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Caitlin
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: With no children of her own, she moved here full-time after her husband's passing. I am grateful for her. I love the boy, but I am no mother.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Darragh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Mister Hunter acts as both the stable master and groundsman, yes?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Darragh
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: The man is a powerhouse. He does the work of five men around here. I have offered to bring in some support for him, but he loves the work - and the solitude it provides.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Seamus
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Has the porter, Mister Doyle, been here long?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Seamus
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: No - nor do I see him staying here much longer.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Seamus
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: The staff are like a family to one another, but he does not seem to feel that way. I do not need friction under my roof.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Please, Marquess, tell me about yourself?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I am the ninth Marquess of Doon, for a start.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: But the first to open the building to outsiders.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: What is there to say? I am a dedicated father, devoted husband, a man of God, and the host for this séance.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Coventry
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you met with Mister Coventry?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Coventry
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I have tried to meet with each of the event's guests. Mister Coventry's reason for being here mirrors my own - he has lost a wife.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Coventry
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Hopefully, he too, gets what he wants from the séance.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on O Finn
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you met with Mister Ó Finn?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on O Finn
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: That's the mountain man, yes? Not yet, but I intend to speak with him before the séance.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Mantovanni
speaker: Mister Ward
en: How did you hear about Miss Mantovani?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Mantovanni
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: In the same way, one learns of any expert - I asked for recommendations. Her name came at the top of most lists, and so I contacted her.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Mantovanni
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: She has proven a delight, and I have the utmost faith in her for the task she undertakes.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you know Miss Callaghan?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Fiadh
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: The local witch? I have heard of her, of course. Her name always comes up when a crop fails or an animal is sick. The locals call her in to fix things.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Fiadh
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I turn a blind eye - they are entitled to handle things as they see fit.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Fiadh
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I had considered her as a host for this event but based on what I know of the woman, she would have turned me down.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Dupre
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you know who Mister Dupré is?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Dupre
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Ah yes. The voodoo undertaker. It is flattering that he has come so far for us. I hope he enjoys his time here.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Darcy
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you know Missus D'Arcy?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Darcy
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Only by name, through her husband. It's a shame he did not join us - I'm told he's quite the accomplished magus.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Father sinnot
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you met the priest, Father Sinnott?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Father sinnot
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I am ashamed to say that the few times we have spoken have been... stilted. In truth, I have never spoken to a Catholic priest before and find him... intimidating.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Father sinnot
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I hope we can find a way to converse outside of that. I am sure he has much to share that is of value - if only I can find a way to pull it from him.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Cathal
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you had time to talk with Cathal O'Meara?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Cathal
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: He is the one obsessed with angels, yes? That surprised me. I've had dealings with his uncle, and he, at least, seemed perfectly grounded.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Hazel
speaker: Mister Ward
en: You've met Missus Erickson, I assume?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Hazel
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I... perhaps. I have met a lot of people. She must not have made much of an impression.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Ettiene
speaker: Mister Ward
en: It must be surprising to have somebody like Mister Toussaint here?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Ettiene
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: The debunker? Yes, well - I believe we have the best chance of achieving our goal when all minds are attuned to it.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Ettiene
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: His presence, I fear, might be like a person singing out of key in a choir - or singing a different song entirely.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Ettiene
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: A distraction for the rest and a sour overall experience.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Ettiene
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: ...Perhaps he is the reason our gauge has dropped? Hmmm...

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Arwa
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Has Miss Hisham spoken with you?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Arwa
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: She is the lady looking for reparations for past deeds, is she not?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Arwa
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: How gauche to bring it up here and now. Does she not care for our greater aim here? She could come and berate me any other week, but not now.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Ruairí
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Doctor Callaghan is from the area. Do you know him?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Ruairí
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Not especially, but I am glad he has come. I gather his talents are suitably impressive.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Ines
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Has Miss Barbosa talked with you?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Ines
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Hmmm? Oh yes. If she were not from the far side of the world, I would have forgotten her entirely.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Ines
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: How she ended up here, I do not know. She is quite clear that the event holds little interest to her.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Saoirse
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Miss Murphy, has she been with you long?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Saoirse
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: A few years. She all but grew up here. She became a woman here, too - sadly. The less said about that, the better.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Saoirse
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: But that mistake is behind her now, and she has been given a second chance. The good Lord does not grant a third.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Walter
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I've not yet had the pleasure of meeting your son.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Walter
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Nor will you. With respect, Sir, I do not think this event is suitable for him - too many strange ideas for his young mind.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Walter
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: It is bad enough that I have strayed down this path. If my wildest dreams come true and I see my wife, then... I will be fit to deal with whatever that does to me.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Walter
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: But he is just a boy. I fear what seeing her like that might do to him. Or not seeing her - that, too, would be hard on him.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Walter
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I would do anything to protect that boy - and so I have ordered him to stay in our residence until this whole ordeal is over.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Deane
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you spoken much with Miss Deane?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Character Presents - Blake/Opinion on Deane
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: She left before we'd had a chance to be introduced. A shame - I gather she is quite the woman, and a capable practitioner of her art.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Analysis Presents - (to) Blake/Tired shoulders - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: You look to be carrying the world upon your shoulders, Marquess.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Analysis Presents - (to) Blake/Tired shoulders - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Hmmm. These last few years have not been easy. But that will all be in the past, soon. A new day, a new chapter, is only hours away.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Analysis Presents - (to) Blake/Haunted expression - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: You seem worried. Is everything alright?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Analysis Presents - (to) Blake/Haunted expression - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Do I now? I suppose it is fair to say that I have a lot riding on this event.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Analysis Presents - (to) Blake/Haunted expression - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Once it is done, it will be nice to return to the way things were and relax for a spell.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Analysis Presents - (to) Blake/Proud Stature - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: It must be a great privilege to be the Marquess of Doon.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Analysis Presents - (to) Blake/Proud Stature - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: It is but, I cannot lie, the title means less nowadays. The family is smaller, the holdings smaller, still.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Analysis Presents - (to) Blake/Proud Stature - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: It is my hope that turning the manor into a hotel and hosting this event will play their parts in reinvigorating the role, before I pass it on to Walter.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Analysis Presents - (to) Blake/watch - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Keeping an eye on the time, Marquess?

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Analysis Presents - (to) Blake/watch - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: This séance has been in planning for some time now. As we near the séance itself, it feels as if time is slowing.

conversation: Cast/Jonathan Blake/Analysis Presents - (to) Blake/watch - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I am most eager to get to it.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley tells you to sign in
speaker: Mister Varley
en: Yes?

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley tells you to sign in
speaker: Mister Varley
en: We did not receive your message, Mister Ward. Our telegraph machine is broken.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley tells you to sign in
speaker: Mister Varley
en: Regardless. I am Vincent Varley, the manager here. We are quite full at present, but we can fit you in.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley tells you to sign in
speaker: Mister Varley
en: I'll send word that a room should be prepared, and I'll show you to it as soon as is possible. It shall be no later than midnight.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley tells you to sign in
speaker: Mister Varley
en: But first, we require our guests to sign in. If you would...

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley tells you to sign in
speaker: Mister Varley
en: The book, Mister Ward, if you would...

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley tells you to sign in
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Hello. I'm Declan Ward. I telegrammed ahead.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley tells you to sign in
speaker: Mister Varley
en: Yes, we received your message. You failed to mention the late hour of your arrival.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley tells you to sign in
speaker: Mister Varley
en: I've been trying to replace the battery. Were it not for that, I'd have locked up by now.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley tells you to sign in
speaker: Mister Varley
en: Now. Mister Ward, was it?

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley tells you to sign in
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Yes. I telegrammed ahead.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley tells you to sign in
speaker: Mister Varley
en: I see.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley tells you to sign in
speaker: Mister Varley
en: I wouldn't be up at this hour, but I've been trying to replace the battery in the thing. If it were not for that, I'd have locked up before now.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Mister Varley
en: May I be of service, Mister Ward?

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Detective Ward
en: LEAVE

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I need nothing else, thank you.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Mister Varley
en: Certainly.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Mister Varley
en: Then I shall return to my office. If you need me again, no doubt you know how to summon me.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Mister Varley
en: This way, Sir.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Mister Varley
en: Then please wait here. The staff will prepare your room, and I'll be back to show you to it shortly.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Mister Varley
en: Mister Ward. I do hope the earlier commotion with the bird didn't disturb your rest?

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Mister Varley
en: Is there anything else I can help with?

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Mister Varley
en: And your fellow guests will be giving talks throughout the day in the drawing room, located in the west corridor.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Detective Ward
en: CONFRONT!

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Mister Varley
en: ...Yes. I regret to say it, but you're right.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Mister Varley
en: Do not get me wrong - I am concerned for Miss Deane. But I have done what I can, and still cannot find her.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Mister Varley
en: This séance, the Marquess' obsession, and the money spent... We need this event to go well or we are homeless.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Mister Varley
en: Now. If you will excuse me. With the telegraph machine broken, I have delivery orders to write for the morning.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Mister Varley
en: If you need me again, you know how to summon me.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Mister Varley
en: Thank you for bringing this to my attention. Your room should be ready soon, and I'll show you to it then.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Mister Varley
en: Now, if you'll excuse me, I have some messages to send before then.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Mister Varley
en: If that's true, and that stash of gold is somewhere on the grounds, then finding it might just be enough to save the hotel.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Mister Varley
en: Take this - it was found in what remained of the lady's personal belongings, but I've never discovered what it unlocks. It's not much, but it's a start.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Mister Varley
en: I've had no luck, obviously. But you... you might be able to find it.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Mister Ward
en: It's certainly possible. If that will stop you from hindering this investigation, then I will see if I can help.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Mister Varley
en: You see... There are rumours of treasure somewhere on the estate - a cache of gold from the mid-to-late 1600s.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Mister Varley
en: Grainne, the wife of the original Marquess, Edward Blake - she did not... choose to be with him.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Mister Varley
en: There is breakfast in the dining hall from 9am, located in the east corridor here.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Mister Varley
en: She had hoarded a sum of money, intending to use it to escape her husband...

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Mister Varley
en: ...she stabbed him in his sleep, but he awoke and managed to live long enough to kill her.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Mister Varley
en: They died together, and the treasure has not since been found.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Sir, you have not done what you could!

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Mister Ward
en: You hid her disappearance - if you had alerted the police, then a proper search of this place could have been undertaken.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Something may well have happened, or happen to her yet, because of your meddling.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Mister Varley

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Mister Varley
en: You're right, of course.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Mister Varley
en: This place, this hotel. It's not just a business - for the staff, it is our home.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Mister Varley
en: And if Miss Deane's situation had gotten out, we would most assuredly be in trouble.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Varley conversation
speaker: Mister Varley
en: But there might be another way, one that frees us from the fate of this séance...

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Hiring Telegram - Varley
speaker: Mister Ward
en: ...at present, mainly this letter. But once I ask around I should soon learn it there is somethi--

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Hiring Telegram - Varley
speaker: Mister Varley
en: And on what authority are you carrying out this investigation?

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Hiring Telegram - Varley
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I was asked to come here and ensure Miss Deane is okay.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Hiring Telegram - Varley
speaker: Mister Varley
en: I see. And what makes you think she is not?

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Hiring Telegram - Varley
speaker: Mister Varley
en: I have no choice but to ask you to leave. Go.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Hiring Telegram - Varley
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I... Nothing official...

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Hiring Telegram - Varley
speaker: Mister Varley
en: Well then. I cannot have you interfering with this event, worrying our guests with idle speculation when they are trying to focus their minds.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Cash - Varley
speaker: Mister Varley
en: You can settle any charges at the front desk, Mister Ward.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Cash - Varley
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ OFFER MONEY ]

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Cash - Varley
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ KEEP MONEY ]

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Cash - Varley
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I'll hold onto this for now.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Photograph of Miss Deane - Varley
speaker: Mister Varley
en: Ah. Miss Evelyn Deane. Taken in our drawing room, I think.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Luggage - Varley
speaker: Mister Varley
en: You may deposit your luggage on the rack to my right.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Luggage - Varley
speaker: Mister Varley
en: You may deposit your luggage on the rack in the lobby.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Luggage - Varley
speaker: Mister Varley
en: Our porter will then bring it to your room when ready.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Luggage - Varley
speaker: Detective Ward
en: I am sorry about the late hour...

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Luggage - Varley
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I am sorry about the late hour... I misjudged the time needed for the journey.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Luggage - Varley
speaker: Mister Varley
en: It happens often enough. If we'd known you were coming, we would have been happy to send the coach out for you.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Luggage - Varley
speaker: Mister Varley
en: The driver knows the route well enough to take some time off the trip.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Luggage - Varley
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Perhaps for my departure.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Luggage - Varley
speaker: Mister Varley
en: Perhaps.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Luggage - Varley
speaker: Mister Varley
en: It happens often enough. Though usually not so late in the day.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Luggage - Varley
speaker: Mister Varley
en: Our driver knows the routes well. He would shorten your return trip.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/Luggage - Varley
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I will keep that in mind, thanks.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/A Map of the Region - Varley
speaker: Mister Varley
en: If you intend on some sightseeing while in the area, our stablemaster is on hand to bring you around.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/A Map of the Region - Varley
speaker: Detective Ward
en: What amenities does the hotel offer?

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/A Map of the Region - Varley
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What can you tell me about the hotel's amenities?

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/A Map of the Region - Varley
speaker: Mister Varley
en: Breakfast, lunch, and dinner are served in the dining room.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/A Map of the Region - Varley
speaker: Mister Varley
en: And usually, we have the telegraph room for communication. I am sure it will be repaired soon.

conversation: Cast/Vincent Varley/Evidence Presents - Varley/A Map of the Region - Varley
speaker: Mister Varley
