en: But I have some renown as a poet. I'll find the money for my sisters' dowries that way, and I will work for my living.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Corentine conversation
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: We are going to be okay. I will see to it. I got us this far. And I suppose you did too, in the end - so thank you, Mister Ward.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Corentine conversation
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: No, none of it will be easy. But it will be worth it. After all - for the first time in my life, I have a future.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Corentine conversation
speaker: Detective Ward
en: How does she feel having lifted the curse?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Corentine conversation
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: What? Listen, Sir, I don't want to... Unless you have that book, I am afraid I just don't have time to talk...

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Research book - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Wait, you - hah! Look at that, you do indeed. Where was it?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Research book - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: But for now... Thank you, sincerely - and do please excuse me. I have work to do.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Research book - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Page seventy-eight, and... That's what I was looking for.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Research book - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Anyhow - I'm pleased to meet you, Mister Ward. My name is Corentine Quinn. You can call me Corentine, and I might, now, owe you a favour.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Research book - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I don't think... I haven't seen you before the incident with the bird. Unless I'm wrong...?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Research book - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Rest assured, Miss, we haven't met. My name's Declan Ward - I've only arrived recently.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Research book - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Even then, I could still have missed you. If you hadn't come by the library, I mean.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Research book - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Actually, I believe I might have the records you are looking for.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Research book - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Miss Barbosa had it.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Research book - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Of course! I loaned it to her during tea and then forgot - too many late nights researching. Speaking of which...

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Research book - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Thank you, Sir, you've helped me a lot. I-I don't know why you would, but you have.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Research book - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: ...How did she get it--

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Photograph of Deane - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you recognise this woman, Miss?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Photograph of Deane - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: ... That's Evelyn Deane.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Photograph of Deane - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: She was around here a few days ago, though where she's gone now, I don't know.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Photograph of Deane - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you know her?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Photograph of Deane - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: We were friends, once... at least while I was useful to her. I am not anymore. We don't talk.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Photograph of Deane - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I'm... sorry to hear that, Miss.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Photograph of Deane - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Well, it's not your fault.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Photograph of Deane - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: But that photograph, it is Evelyn Deane, and it can't be very old.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Photograph of Deane - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Sir, I'm really quite busy.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Map of the Region - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: It's a local map... Ah, but mostly geographical.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Staff area key - Corentine

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/News clippings - Corentine

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Telegram draft - Corentine

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Written complaint - Corentine

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Talks schedule - Corentine

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Talks schedule - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Talks schedule - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Journal Entry about Miss Quinn - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I gather you and Miss Deane had a falling out of sorts?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Journal Entry about Miss Quinn - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I do not make friends easily, Mister Ward. I have a great deal of responsibilities and I am left with little time for socialising.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Journal Entry about Miss Quinn - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Evelyn came to me for help deciphering a grimoire - an ancient tome of spells - that being my speciality.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Journal Entry about Miss Quinn - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I suppose that is a way to describe it.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Journal Entry about Miss Quinn - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I liked her. She was curious and sharp. And she was exciting to be around. Chaotic, which was a nice break from how ordered the rest of my life was.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Journal Entry about Miss Quinn - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: We fast became friends.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Journal Entry about Miss Quinn - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Then one of her friends in the order showed up with a Sufi who had, or claimed to have, an original copy of The Picatrix, with annotations not copied into later editions.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Journal Entry about Miss Quinn - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: She had to see it, of course. And all she needed to do was to steal them some of my books as payment.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Journal Entry about Miss Quinn - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: To stop me coming after her, I suppose. I couldn't, though. I was heartbroken. I washed my hands of it all and returned to my work.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Journal Entry about Miss Quinn - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I would have been wiser to stick to my books in the first place.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Journal Entry about Miss Quinn - Corentine

speaker: Miss Quinn

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Fetters - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: They are the ties that bind, if you will. Something of such emotional significance to a soul, for whatever reason, that they cannot leave it.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Fetters - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Thus, their reason for remaining in our world, against their will or otherwise.

en: What else? There's more ritual - they believe in transubstantiation, which is quite the concept.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Catholic Faith - Corentine

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Catholic Faith - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: But as you might have gathered, I am not Catholic, nor especially godly, so I am perhaps not the person to ask if you want a comprehensive answer.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Protestant Faith - Corentine

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Protestant Faith - Corentine

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Protestant Faith - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: But my faith is mostly a matter of tradition and culture. I don't put an awful lot of stock in it.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Protestant Faith - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: It's a curious idea, and perhaps a nice one, but not something I'd stake all hope in.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Ettiene's Influence - Corentine

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Ettiene's Influence - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I'm not interested in showmanship and splendour. I'm a scholar. If I were a charlatan, I'd be a very poor one.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Ettiene's Influence - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I'm not making any money or finding any glory spending my time in these books, you know.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Strange dream - Corentine

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Strange dream - Corentine

en: You've experienced it then?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Strange dream - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Ritual complete
speaker: Mister Ward
en: With the ritual complete, am I to understand that the Quinn family is free of their curse?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Ritual complete
speaker: Miss Quinn

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Ritual complete
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Finally. Finally.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Ritual complete
speaker: Mister Ward

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Ritual complete
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Oh, almost everything - we will be significantly poorer, there's no doubt about that. It will not be easy.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Ritual complete
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: But I have some renown as a poet. I'll find the money for my sisters' dowries that way, and I will work for my living.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Ritual complete
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: We are going to be okay. I will see to it. I got us this far. And after all... For the first time in our lives, we have a future to plan for.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Hedonistic Gala - Corentine

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Hedonistic Gala - Corentine

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Hedonistic Gala - Corentine

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Curse - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I'd ask why you'd dwell on such a thing - but terrible things inspire curiosity, I think. Look, I will put it to bed for you, and then we can be done with it.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Curse - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: My ancestors - at least, a crucial few of them - were awful people. People who valued wealth over other people.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Curse - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: They were Catholic, you see, and so knew of many other Catholics in a time when it was outlawed.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Curse - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: They turned these other families over to the crown and were rewarded for it. But it's not like it went unnoticed.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Curse - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: So they were cursed for it in retribution; cursed with terrible and early fates, with, in general, grave misfortune.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Curse - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: And, as it turns out, it followed the bloodline. So, one hundred years removed, I am one of the only three remaining Quinns.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Curse - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I have lost my parents, my aunts and uncles, my cousins, and my siblings - bar, thank God, two.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Curse - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I've dedicated myself to learning how to break this curse to save us. I became a damned master of my craft to do so.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Curse - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: My ancestors - at least, a crucial few of them - were awful people. People who valued wealth over others' lives.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Curse - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: And, well, they turned many of those over to the crown for coin.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Curse - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: So they were cursed for it; cursed with terrible and early fates, along with, in general, grave misfortune.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Curse - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: And, as it turns out, the curse followed the bloodline. So, less than one hundred years removed, I am one of the only three remaining Quinns.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Curse - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I have lost my parents, my aunts and uncles, my cousins, and my siblings - bar two, thank God.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Curse - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I've dedicated myself to learning how to break this curse and save us - I've become a damned master of my craft-

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Curse - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: And now it's come to this. Learning the name of the spirit I need to appease, and finding myself unable to reach her.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Curse - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Is that enough? Have I made the tragedy clear for you?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Curse - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: And in the end - it took you, asking questions where you probably should not have been.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Curse - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I don't know what my life will look like now, Mister Ward, or what sort of home I will have for myself...

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Curse - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: But if you ever find yourself in my part of England, and don't mind modest means, you should come by. You've earned a lifetime of warm welcomes.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Curse - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: What stupid, meaningless deaths.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Curse - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: They were Catholic, you see, and knew many other Catholics - including some wanted by the Crown.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Curse - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: But it's not like it went unnoticed.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Curse - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: ...and still, it remains.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Curse - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: What stupid, meaningless deaths.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Curse - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: All for some coin and comfort.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Shay O'Connor - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Miss Barbosa's father was named Seamus O'Connor, it turns out.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Shay O'Connor - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: She found it, then? I am glad for her. Good to see my research put to even more positive use.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/well scrying - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What do you know about well scrying?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/well scrying - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: It's an Irish tradition, gazing into a well and asking for answers.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/well scrying - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: It doesn't seem to have transferred to England like you might expect of a mostly secular spiritual practice.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/well scrying - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: It might be that it only works, at least as it's known, in Ireland. I wonder...

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/well scrying - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Miss Callaghan was kind enough to lead me in a session. I wanted to see that my sisters were well.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/well scrying - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I trust they are?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/well scrying - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Yes. When I saw them, they seemed fine, thank God.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/well scrying - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Can I ask you what has you out here?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/well scrying - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Ah, I thought I heard someone. It was you, then?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/well scrying - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: We're well scrying. Someone with the right aptitude can look into a well and receive visions. Usually even of the sort they request.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/well scrying - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: And you are one of these people, with the right sort of aptitude?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/well scrying - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: To everyone's astonishment, I'm sure.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/well scrying - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Forgive me, but I overheard some of your conversation with Miss Callaghan, earlier.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/well scrying - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Is that so?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/well scrying - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: May I ask you what you were talking about?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/well scrying - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I... suppose it's no harm. We were scrying. I wanted to see that my sisters were well.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/well scrying - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I trust they are?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/well scrying - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Yes. When I saw them, they seemed fine, thank God.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/well scrying - Corentine
speaker: Detective Ward
en: What is she doing out here?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/well scrying - Corentine
speaker: Detective Ward
en: What was she talking about with Miss Callaghan at the well?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/well scrying - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I have arranged a session with Miss Callaghan. I want to check on family.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/strange paper - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Did you leave this behind in the library, Miss Quinn?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/strange paper - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: That is my handwriting, certainly. It looks like... Ah, it's one of my notes. Magical theory.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/strange paper - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: But I'm beyond the theorising part, now...

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/book of crests - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: There's a book of Irish family crests in the library.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/book of crests - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: The Quinn family crest has a pegasus on it. I was always very proud of that when I was small.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/book of crests - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Usually, you can identify crests by the main imagery. There will be one image or motif that gets used on all sorts of things.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/book of crests - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: People used to care more about that sort of thing.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Deane's room - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you know which room Miss Deane was staying in?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Deane's room - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Mm, if I did at one point, I don't recall now. She must have been near me, though. How strange... It doesn't seem likely I would forget that...

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Enochian magic
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you happen to know anything about Enochian magic?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Enochian magic
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I can't say angels are my forté. If anything, I seem to be attended by a distinct lack of them.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Enochian magic
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: But that's not the case for all of the guests here... have you been speaking to Mister O'Meara?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Enochian magic
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: He's something of a known quantity when it comes to that sort of thing. I don't know of anyone who's quite so... invested in the discipline.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Enochian magic
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Better the discipline, though, than his other exploits. Angels only attend the sides of those that need them, after all.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Enochian magic
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: So he's known to engineer situations for himself in which the angel would appear. Life and death...

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Enochian magic
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: A ridiculous privilege of a venture, to choose to look death in the eyes. But I suppose you can, knowing it's not on your heels.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Enochian magic
speaker: Miss Quinn

en: Do you happen to recognise this, Miss Quinn?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Magical Grimoire - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: ...You know, I'd like to know where you found this, Mister Ward.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Magical Grimoire - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Magical Grimoire - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I'd forget you saw it before some, or all of us, get hurt.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Coded Papers - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do these dots mean anything to you Miss Quinn?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Coded Papers - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: ...It looks to me like a hidden message. Magically hidden, I mean.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Coded Papers - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: You'd need some sort of pattern to show it up - though I suspect only the caster knows what it is.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Coded Papers - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: It's probably something important to them. Or something they'd be able to remember, anyway.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Chimney Charm - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I found this on the grounds. What do you make of it?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Chimney Charm - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: It looks like a charm of some sort. Old, low magic, I'd imagine. But it doesn't look like anything I do, so I couldn't tell you much more than that.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Witchcraft Components- Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What do you make of this? Are they components for a charm or ritual of some sort?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Witchcraft Components- Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Hm. It does look to be something like that. My guess would be it's a traditional charm of some sort. Old magic, you know?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/timetable - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Truthfully, I think anyone would have a hard time getting me out of the library this weekend, Mister Ward.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/timetable - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I wish I could spend another day in the library again, but I cannot.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/timetable - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What's this weekend looking like for you, Miss Quinn?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/timetable - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Anything exciting planned for today?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/timetable - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Otherwise, I've Miss Mantovani's talk at five and dinner at seven. As for tomorrow...

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/timetable - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I suppose some variety would be good for me. I'll be in church for the service at noon and, after some time in the graveyard, I have lunch at one.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/timetable - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I'm also seeing Doctor Callaghan's talk at three. I've yet to decide what I'll do between it and attending the silent dinner at eight.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/timetable - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Which then brings us to the séance at 9pm. I'm eager to see Miss Mantovani work.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/timetable - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I'm planning to enjoy the library again all day, and perhaps the graveyard too. Go ahead and marvel at my whimsy.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/timetable - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I'll be sitting the séance out in my room.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/End of quest - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: With the ritual complete, am I to understand that the Quinn family is free of their curse?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/End of quest - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I've instructed my solicitor to transfer all the deeds to Miss Barbosa. If 'Biddy' O'Connor keeps her word... yes, I think it's done.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/End of quest - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Finally. Finally.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/End of quest - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: If I might ask... will you and your family be alright? Losing that much land and the money from it must mean you're losing most of your assets.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/End of quest - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Oh, almost everything - we will be significantly poorer, there's no doubt about that. It will not be easy.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/End of quest - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: But I have some renown as a poet. I'll find the money for my sisters' dowries that way, and I will work for my living.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/End of quest - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: We are going to be okay. I will see to it. I got us this far. And I suppose you did too, in the end - so thank you, Mister Ward.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/End of quest - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: No, none of it will be easy. But it will be worth it. After all - for the first time in my life, I have a future.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Ivy and Darragh - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Were you aware that Miss McLeod and Mister Hunter are close?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Ivy and Darragh - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I can't say I know either of them well enough to be privy to that sort of thing, no. But I suppose I do now.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Ivy and Darragh - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Funny. We all try so hard to seem good and proper, and almost no one is. And for good reason. What do we gain, being proper?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Ivy and Darragh - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Just the denial of things that make life bearable. The denial of a dear friendship or a moment's respite...

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Ivy and Darragh - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: The world is ridiculous.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Blackmail letter - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What do you make of this?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Blackmail letter - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Ugh... Good God, that's low, even for Evelyn.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Blackmail letter - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I don't know what your opinions on these matters are, Mister Ward, but look at it this way.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Blackmail letter - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Of all those involved in this, only Evelyn is doing anyone any harm. I would suggest you keep this to yourself, lest you start a scandal.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/Blackmail letter - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Surely Miss McLeod being blackmailed into service is enough for them to contend with just for now... Don't you think?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/gauge - corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you seen the strange device, the one with the green jar, in the atrium?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/gauge - corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Even I am not distracted enough to miss that. It looks impressive, but without knowing much about it, that is all I can say.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/washer woman - quinn
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I've seen her, yes. She's a bean nigh. A spirit of warning.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/washer woman - quinn
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you spotted a woman washing clothes in any strange places?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/washer woman - quinn
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Whoever's clothes she washes is fated to die. I do not know if it is preventable.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/washer woman - quinn
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: But just in case, I have been trying to figure out whose clothes I saw her wash.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Evidence Presents - Corentine/washer woman - quinn
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: But I have had no luck. In my defence, I have been largely preoccupied with saving my own, first and foremost.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Skerritt - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you know Mister Skerritt?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Skerritt - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I do. He's one of the wealthiest men in London. The last of an old banking family. In my position, it would be hard not to know him.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Skerritt - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: He seemed... disinterested, once he had the scope of me, though. And I am no worse for it.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Skerritt - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Sir, I'm really quite busy.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Lan Fen - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you had the chance to speak with Missus Lau?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Lan Fen - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: She seems canny - though somewhat out of place, being a regular academic.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Lan Fen - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: We had a lively exchange about her work, but her expression shifted as Miss Deane passed us by.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Lan Fen - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Sir, I'm really quite busy.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Lan Fen - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Though I cannot claim to speak for Missus Lau, in that moment, her eyes spoke volumes.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Lan Fen - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I wouldn’t be the least bit surprised if she and Miss Deane had some sour dealings in the past.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Lan Fen - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Something we share, her and I.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Ivy - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I suppose you've met Miss McLeod?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Ivy - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I have. For all the people I've met who wrongfully claim to see the future... I think I believe her.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Ivy - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: She's got spirit. Charming, too. I'm inclined to like her.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Ivy - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Sir, I'm really quite busy.

speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Only about getting some more writing paper.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Varley - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Sir, I'm really quite busy.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Varley - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: He’s not much for small talk, but he certainly puts in the effort to accommodate his guests who lean towards the arts.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Varley - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I heard he placed a Gramophone inside Mister Toussaint’s room upon request, and the other day I saw him carrying paint supplies to Mister Coventry’s room.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Caitlin - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you spoken to the housekeeper?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Caitlin - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Only a little. She asked me where I was visiting from.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Caitlin - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Though why she wanted to know, I couldn't say... There are people here from more interesting places.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Caitlin - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you spoken to the housekeeper?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Caitlin - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: ... It might be more accurate to say that the housekeeper has spoken to me.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Caitlin - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: She spent ten minutes cautioning me on the health hazards of being near Miss Mantovani - and also in libraries.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Caitlin - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I don't recall that I ever responded.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Seamus - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Did you happen to have met the porter?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Seamus - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Of course. He carried my bags in. Thankfully, there was very little that was delicate in them, as he kept dropping them.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Seamus - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: He was very sorry about it, but it was clear he was... wasn't all there.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Seamus - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: One of my cousins died from an overreliance on drugs and, well... Mister Doyle should probably clean up his act...

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Darragh - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you met the stable master?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Darragh - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: He's spoken with me whenever I visited the horses. I was there to talk to the actual horses, mind you.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Darragh - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Sir, I'm really quite busy.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Darragh - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I did hear him mutter something about Deane, which I took to mean Miss Deane - I have yet to meet a person she hasn't rubbed the wrong way!

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Corentine - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What can you tell me about yourself, Miss Quinn?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Corentine - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Mm. Let's see.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Corentine - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I am a poet by trade, and I have had some success with it. I am twenty-five, traditionally qualified, and the head of my household.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Corentine - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: That being for lack of anyone more traditionally qualified, you understand.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Corentine - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: ...and I am a scholar of grimoire magic, which is to say I study it rather than rely on a divine source. How does that do?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Evelyn - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What do you know of Miss Deane?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Evelyn - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Oh, you know... Irish, of a certain class, interested in mysticism... most branches, rather than one in particular.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Evelyn - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I don't know what she does these days. I only know it's not grimoire magic, because that was why she first spoke to me.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Evelyn - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Sir, I'm really quite busy.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Evelyn - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: She learned her lot and decided it wasn't for her. Now I hear she's a member of the Hermetic Order Of The Golden Dawn.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Evelyn - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: You'd have to ask another of them to know for sure, of course.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Evelyn - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: But frankly, you'd do better asking someone else. Evelyn and I haven't been on speaking terms for some time.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Evelyn - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I don't know what she does these days, but when we met, she was hunting for ancient secrets in grimoires.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Ettiene - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you met Mister Touissant?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Ettiene - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: It's the first opportunity I've had to put a face to the name - I made time to make my introductions.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Ettiene - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: You're pleased to see him?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Ettiene - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I respect him, and I respect his work. And, as I hear, he's perfectly decent about it. I haven't heard him hurling baseless accusations yet.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Ettiene - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: He does important work, Mister Ward. Anyone who tries to tell you there are no charlatans in the field deserves a good, hard look themselves.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Ines - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you have cause to speak with Miss Barbosa?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Ines - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Mm... cause? No. But I ended up beside her at tea one day, and she is, dare I say, good fun.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Ines - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Over here because of an Irish father, so she says... Funny, how even after they've passed, your family can take you all sorts of places.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Cathal - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I don't suppose you know Mister O'Meara?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Cathal - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: No, but I know enough to know his type. Born rich, never worked for anything, spends daddy's money on new ways to feel alive.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Cathal - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I tried to tell him I'm sure it was my fault, but he was very apologetic all the same.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Cathal - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Anyhow, we talked, somewhat, after that, so to answer your question, yes.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Cathal - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: He is, perhaps, peculiar, but only in exactly the way you'd expect of an event like this. I take him to be quite amicable. Quite sweet, actually.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Cathal - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: That man has hardly a thought for the world around him. I might sympathise, under different circumstances.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Cathal - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: But as it is... You know, I think I would like him quite a lot, were he less hellbent on wasting a perfectly decent life.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Cathal - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: It's not perfect, I'm sure, but I have no doubt it's not worth throwing away in some stupid, avoidable accident he'll engineer for himself.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Cathal - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: A waste of a life and a perfectly decent man, frankly. He's quite sweet when you manage to get past it all.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Cathal - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I've heard of his antics, and unless he changes his ways, it'll not be long before he's the ghost loved ones are trying to reach...

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Dupré - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you met Mister Dupré?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Dupré - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Well, I haven't been much for talking, but I've been trying to make the time.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Dupré - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: He's very friendly, which is rare to see, and if I'm to be honest with you, I like that about a person.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Dupré - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: The formality demanded by proper acquaintanceship gets so damn dull.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Dupré - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: So, for what little time I have for it, I welcome friendly conversation. And thus, I find I also welcome Mister Dupré.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Dupré - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Besides, I'm too morbid for most, and he has a higher tolerance for that sort of thing.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on D'Arcy - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Did you happen to meet Missus D'Arcy?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on D'Arcy - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Why, when I heard Olivia D'Arcy was here, I had to make some sort of introduction.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on D'Arcy - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: My younger sister and I so enjoyed her debut novel, she wouldn't have forgiven me if I hadn't said hello.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on D'Arcy - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: She's a charming woman. Just as wry as one would expect, and besides - it's always nice to meet another author.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Coventry - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you had the opportunity to meet Mister Coventry?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Coventry - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I have. I would have assumed we'd not have much to talk about - he's no magician, not gentry, and no writer.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Coventry - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: ...Which makes me sound very snobby, but I simply mean I don't have much else I can talk on.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Coventry - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: But he knew of my poetry, and we discussed that for a while.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Coventry - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: It was very distracting, honestly.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Hazel - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you spoken to Missus Erickson?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Hazel - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Not really. She said hello, but I'm so busy...

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Hazel - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I will have to at some point, though. I keep running into her.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Hazel - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I just... hers is a style of occultism that I find very... shallow?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Ruairí - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you met Doctor Callaghan?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Ruairí - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Ah, yes. I do like it when the scientists pitch in - once they accept certain supernatural details, of course. It makes for interesting conversation.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Ruairí - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: A shame for me that he is so focused on the future - he wasn't able to help me much with my search into the past.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Carmela - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you met Miss Mantovani?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Carmela - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I've seen her in London before, though we didn't speak.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Carmela - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: She was quiet when we talked here, but she didn't stay for long. She had a look in her eyes... a sadness.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Carmela - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I don't see that often in the eyes of talented mystics. Usually, they have seen so much that they show nothing.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Blake - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you know the Marquess?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Blake - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: No, I do not. Some of my family knew of him, so I had an impression of the man.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Blake - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Studious, hard working, quiet - a devout protestant.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Blake - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I gather his father spent a generous portion of the family fortune on a lavish lifestyle across Europe - all while Ireland struggled through the famine.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Blake - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: And so, he tasked himself with rebuilding the family's funds by turning the place into a hotel.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Blake - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: But the man I met now - the one who opened his doors to this gathering, this event... - well, there is a gulf between the man I heard of and the one I met here.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Ó Finn - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I don't suppose you've had the opportunity to speak to Mister Ó Finn, have you?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Ó Finn - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: The master of the lands? I did corner him for some information on the people of the region, but he seems more focused on the myths - at some moments, I got the impression he couldn't actually distinguish the two.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Fiadh - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you spoken to Miss Callaghan?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Fiadh - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I have. She is...

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Fiadh - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: She means well, but her eyes are full of pity - and I cannot abide pity.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Fiadh - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I cannot use pity, pity does not set anything right. Only action does.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Father Sinnott - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you met Father Sinnott?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Father Sinnott - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I haven't been especially compelled to introduce myself. Clergymen often disapprove of me.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Father Sinnott - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: As a rule, they dislike vocal women. Or perhaps women as a whole. I've heard of their Magdalene laundries - asylums for anyone found guilty of the crime of being born female.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Father Sinnott - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: So, as intrigued as I am to what business he has here, I will be staying clear.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Arwa - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you made Miss Hisham's acquaintance?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Arwa - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I mean - insomuch as we spoke briefly, but she and I both seem to be occupied, you know?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Arwa - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: She is not. Instead, there is something... disconcerting about her. Something I cannot put my finger on.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Arwa - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Still, she seems like she might make interesting company, if she were in the mood, but...

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Arwa - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Is that how other people feel when they talk to me?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Saoirse - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you spoken to Miss Murphy?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Saoirse - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: That would be... not the housekeeper... Oh, the cook? I haven't said anything in particular to her.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Saoirse - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: She seems nervous around all this well-to-do company - why drag her into a conversation she doesn't wish to be a part of?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Campbell - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you spoken to the Reverend?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Campbell - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: No, and I don't intend to. The last thing I am here for is preaching.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Higgins - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I don't suppose you've seen a man around here - not a guest, but quite a large fellow; he's distinctive.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Higgins - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I can't say I've had eyes for much at all but the contents of the library.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Higgins - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: What might he be doing, if he's not a guest?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Walter Blake - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you know much about Walter Blake?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Character Presents - Corentine/Opinion on Walter Blake - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Not a lot. I've heard of him and gather he is the family's last hope. Frankly, I've been too busy with the survival of my own lot to care too much.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Analysis Presents - (to) Corentine/Well and practically dressed - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: That's quite a striking brooch you have.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Analysis Presents - (to) Corentine/Well and practically dressed - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: My sister gave it to me as a keepsake when I set off. A good luck charm, she called it.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Analysis Presents - (to) Corentine/Well and practically dressed - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I hope that she is right.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Analysis Presents - (to) Corentine/Well and practically dressed - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Given how everything has played out, I think she was right.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Analysis Presents - (to) Corentine/Scars on hands and face - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Forgive me, Miss, but can I ask - how did you end up with the injuries you've sustained?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Analysis Presents - (to) Corentine/Scars on hands and face - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Ah... How do I... Is it enough to say I have terrible luck?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Analysis Presents - (to) Corentine/Scars on hands and face - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: But there is some luck, I suppose, in the fact that I have only been scarred, and it hasn't killed me yet.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Analysis Presents - (to) Corentine/Scars on hands and face - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: You talk like there's something after you.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Analysis Presents - (to) Corentine/Scars on hands and face - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: It does look that way, Mister Ward.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Analysis Presents - (to) Corentine/Pen in pocket - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: You've a pen in your pocket, Miss. Just in case it slipped your mind.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Analysis Presents - (to) Corentine/Pen in pocket - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Oh, don't worry, it's clean. I've stained enough of my clothes not to make that mistake again.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Analysis Presents - (to) Corentine/Pen in pocket - Corentine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I take it you're not often without one.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Analysis Presents - (to) Corentine/Pen in pocket - Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: I'm a poet by trade. I prefer to carry one so I'm never caught with a refrain, or suchlike, and without the means to write it down.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Eavesdrop, overhearing Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Idiots and ghouls, all of you...

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Eavesdrop, overhearing Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: What did you think would happen? That nobody would mind? That they were not entirely as capable of vengeance as you?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Eavesdrop, overhearing Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: And for what? For sixteen funerals in thirty years, but at least - oh, at least the caskets were nice.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Eavesdrop, overhearing Corentine
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: And you never even saw the ruin you caused! It's just me in this godforsaken library! Bastards. What damnable stock we are!

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Corentine's room/Ward evidence comments/Drafted poems
speaker: Mister Ward
en: A collection of half-written poems. I wouldn't know if they're any good, myself...

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Corentine's room/Ward evidence comments/Drafted poems
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Some of them are recent and seem to mention the event and its guests, but those are only fragments.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Corentine's room/Ward evidence comments/Spare pens and paper
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Just some unused writing materials.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Corentine's room/Ward evidence comments/Inscribed locket
speaker: Mister Ward
en: A locket, with two names etched into the inside. Alma and Maurice. And a photograph on the other side, of a young woman and a boy.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Corentine's room/Ward evidence comments/Inscribed locket
speaker: Mister Ward
en: They look quite a lot like Miss Quinn. I suppose they would be her siblings.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Corentine's room/Ward evidence comments/Grimoires
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Grimoires. Most of them printed, one in Miss Quinn's hand, and all of them were annotated and nearly worn out at the spine.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Corentine's room/Ward evidence comments/Grimoires
speaker: Mister Ward
en: It seems they've been used quite extensively over the years, and the handwritten one seems to be the product of enormous time and effort.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Corentine's room/Ward evidence comments/Shoes
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Nothing much to note here.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Corentine's room/Ward evidence comments/Death memento
speaker: Mister Ward
en: A brooch containing a lock of hair. The back says Alexander Quinn, 1865-1896.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Corentine's room/Ward evidence comments/Poetry book
speaker: Mister Ward
en: A published book of Miss Quinn's poetry, with scraps of paper containing annotations and drafts tucked between the pages.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Corentine's room/Ward evidence comments/Poetry book
speaker: Mister Ward
en: It seems to be more to do with her revisions and artistic process than anything relevant to my investigation.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Corentine's room/Ward evidence comments/Jewellery
speaker: Mister Ward
en: A collection of jewellery, mostly quite understated.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Meeting Corentine in the corridor
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Excuse me, would you? I just - I need to think.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Ritual
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: And I appreciate it. Alright. Alright, one more time.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Ritual
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Hear me, 'Biddy' Eve O'Connor, I call you from beyond the grave. Hear me, the child of the family you damned.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Ritual
speaker: Miss Barbosa
en: Santo Cristo! Um fantasma!

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Ritual
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Hear me, so that we may bury all this grief.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Ritual
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Are you 'Biddy' Eve O'Connor?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Ritual
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Good. My name is Corentine Quinn. I am of the third generation of the Quinn family since Fiontan Quinn, and now one of the three of us that remain.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Ritual
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: It is myself, and my two sisters. The people that wronged you - and they did wrong you, I will not deny it - they're long since dead by your curse.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Ritual
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: My ancestors sinned against you, but we did not. For the sake of my life, for my dear sisters' lives, I implore you to release us from your curse.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Ritual
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Would you consider this, now the man who hurt you so is dead?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Ritual
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Excellent, alright. Let me think. Do you require your bones to be laid to rest?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Ritual
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: If too many candles blow out, the ritual will be over, spent, and I will have lost my chance. My family will be doomed.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Ritual
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Do you have some unfinished business here that I could see to on your behalf?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Ritual
speaker: Spirit

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Ritual
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: They betrayed their fellow Catholics to the Crown, and then they took the land- Oh. Oh! Maybe...

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Ritual
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: 'Biddy' O'Connor, you would have me relinquish my claim on that land, the money from it?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Ritual
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: She... Oh, why didn't I see it? - Miss Barbosa - Ines - would you accept the Quinn lands, and the money we made from it?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Ritual
speaker: Miss Barbosa
en: What...?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Ritual
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: It was ill-got, it shouldn't be ours - and if it will satisfy 'Biddy' O'Connor for her descendant to have it... Will you take it? Please?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Ritual
speaker: Miss Barbosa
en: You are serious...

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Ritual
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: 'Biddy' Eve O'Connor, from the bottom of my heart, I offer you my deepest apologies for all the wrong done to you, and my promise, the Quinn fortune will go to Ines Barbosa.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Ritual
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: She can do with it as she likes. I will relinquish every acre and every penny of it immediately. This I swear to you, on my honour and my life.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Ritual
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: And if that's all that need be said, then... Then, I bid you goodbye, 'Biddy' O'Connor, and thank you. May you rest in peace.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Ritual
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Come, Miss Barbosa. We'll go to the telegraph room and send word to my lawyers so they can get the paperwork in order.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Ritual
speaker: Miss Barbosa
en: Huh. Lead the way, I suppose?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Ritual
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: You'll be needed too, Mister Ward, to witness. Come along, would you?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Ritual
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Thank you, Miss Barbosa - this could well save the lives of the last people that truly matter to me.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Ritual
speaker: Miss Barbosa
en: I do not understand how being in a bathroom with two strangers is helping, but I am eager to learn.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Ritual
speaker: Mister Ward

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Ritual
speaker: Spirit

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Ritual
speaker: Miss Quinn

speaker: Spirit

speaker: Miss Barbosa

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Ritual
speaker: Miss Barbosa
en: Tsss... What did your ancestors do to deserve all this?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Ritual
speaker: Miss Quinn

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Ritual
speaker: Spirit

speaker: Miss Barbosa

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Post ritual conversation
speaker: Miss Barbosa

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Post ritual conversation
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Yes, I am sure it is a lot to take in...

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Post ritual conversation
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: But look, that hardly matters now; I'm going to write to my solicitor and have him prepare everything for you. All we will need then is to get the deeds to you.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Post ritual conversation
speaker: Miss Barbosa
en: So, you're serious? It was not a lie to trick the spirit?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Post ritual conversation
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Completely and utterly serious, Miss Barbosa. One does not trick ghosts and come off the better for it.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Post ritual conversation
speaker: Miss Barbosa
en: Ines. Just call me Ines. All this... It's hard to comprehend.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Post ritual conversation
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Well, you have the rest of your life to get your head around it, Ines. And now, so do I.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Post ritual conversation
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: ...And if I am to call you that, then you must call me Corentine. I've always hated "Miss Quinn".

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Post ritual conversation
speaker: Miss Barbosa
en: If you say so, Corentine. Plenty of time to get familiar now, yes?

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Post ritual conversation
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Now. You sign here to prove you accepted them, then you here Mister Ward as witness.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Post ritual conversation
speaker: Miss Quinn
en: Hah! Isn't there just? But you know, I think I am done with summoning the damned. I am going to skip the séance and do something I've not done for some time - think about the future.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Post ritual conversation
speaker: Miss Barbosa
en: As much as I value the lands and wealth, that is the real treasure in all of this.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Post ritual conversation
speaker: Miss Barbosa
en: Very good. And I, I now have my father's real name - Seamus O'Connor.

conversation: Cast/Corentine Quinn/Post ritual conversation
speaker: Miss Barbosa

en: Anyway, cleaning up is the housekeeper's business. Let her know, I guess.

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Cathal saw Deane - Seamus
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Apparently, Miss Deane was seen late Tuesday night, and it seemed as if she'd been drinking.

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Cathal saw Deane - Seamus
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: Haha, I suppose these people aren't quite so high and mighty, eh?

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Cathal saw Deane - Seamus
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: Didn't she leave, then, too? Ugh, I don't envy her that carriage ride with a hangover...

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Waiting on a message - Seamus
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I was talking to Miss Barbosa... Do you think you might have mislaid a message?

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Waiting on a message - Seamus
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: No, I don't think... Even if I have... I'll get to it when I get to it, alright?

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Bedroom skeleton key - Seamus
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: What the hell - ? Why do you... Give that here, would you?

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Strange occurences - Doyle
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you noticed anything strange around this place?

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Strange occurences - Doyle
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: Here? Have you seen anything normal?

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Strange occurences - Doyle
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: The whole place creeps me out. Strange noises, figures in the corner of your eye - then gone. A feeling you're never alone.

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Strange occurences - Doyle
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: Why I came here is a mystery, but why I stay is a bigger one.

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Locker key - Doyle
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you recognise this key?

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Locker key - Doyle
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: Is that the key I gave... You shouldn't have that. The bathhouse is closed, and the lockers are off limits. Throw that back to reception, yeah?

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Statement - Doyle
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Can you tell me anything else about that argument you overheard?

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Statement - Doyle
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: It was erratic. Went from pleading to aggressive and a bit of mockery in there, too.

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Statement - Doyle
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: I didn't catch much, though. I was on the same kinda break you caught me on.

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Statement - Doyle
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: The man might have had an accent... but that might just have been that I was hearing it through the wall.

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Statement - Doyle
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: I mean, it probably wasn't an important argument, you know? Just some high-society rubbish.

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Mysterious figure - Doyle
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I could have sworn I saw a figure in the window when I was heading back to the manor.

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Mysterious figure - Doyle
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: Don't worry about it, Sir.

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Mysterious figure - Doyle
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Any idea who it might have been?

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/The Fae - Doyle
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you know anything about the fae, Mister Doyle?

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/The Fae - Doyle
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: Best not to talk about them, Sir. At least not to call them by name.

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/The Fae - Doyle
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: I met one, once, out on the grounds. I thought maybe he was a guest I hadn't seen yet, but the moment I looked him in the eyes...

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/The Fae - Doyle
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: My own voice asking my name from my own face.

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/The Fae - Doyle
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: And then he asked me for my name.

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/The Fae - Doyle
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: I knew if I stayed, I had given him my name. And I knew if he had that, I'd not be seen again. Not the real me.

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/The Fae - Doyle
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: I never knew until that night how fast my legs could carry me.

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/The old anvil - Doyle
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Is there a story to the old anvil?

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/The old anvil - Doyle
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: Uh, no. No, I don't think... No, there isn't.

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Dead End - Doyle
speaker: Mister Ward
en: It seems Miss Deane didn't leave on Tuesday night. She wandered into the hedge maze, but there's been no sign of her since.

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Dead End - Doyle
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: Wait, what? She... But that doesn't make any sense.

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Dead End - Doyle
speaker: Mister Ward
en: It doesn't, not yet.

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Trinkets - Doyle
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: What use would I have for this?

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Trinkets - Doyle
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ OFFER TRINKET ]

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Trinkets - Doyle
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ KEEP TRINKET ]

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Trinkets - Doyle
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I'll hold onto this for now.

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Entertainment schedule - Seamus
speaker: Mister Ward
en: There's quite the array of pastimes happening this week, I gather.

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Entertainment schedule - Seamus
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: Plenty enough. Plenty enough to keep us on our feet and at work, anyway...

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Bridge game - Seamus
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I understand there was a game of bridge held on Tuesday night.

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Bridge game - Seamus
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: Don't ask me about that. Sure, I already told you I was in the hedge maze listening to your one when that was happen--

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Bridge game - Seamus
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: --Oh! I see what you're doing. Asking in a roundabout way. What are you, some kinda bobby? Ha!

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Bridge game - Seamus
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: Wait... Are you, police? You legally have to tell me if you are. Is that right? Dammit, I'm not sure.

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Arwa statement - Doyle
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I was talking with Miss Hisham, and she mentioned she saw Father Sinnott talking with someone at the gates. Tall and broad, she said.

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Arwa statement - Doyle
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: Did she? Well... 'spose it's not my business what the Father gets up to, is it? It's not hers, either.

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Stall door - Seamus
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I notice one of the stable doors has been recently mended.

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Stall door - Seamus
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: Has it? That'd be Mister Hunter's work, then. He does all the heavy lifting around here - he's well able for it, even at his age.

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Staff area key - Seamus
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: Why do you even have that? You people...

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Front door - Doyle
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do the staff lock the front doors at night?

conversation: Cast/Seamus Doyle/Evidence Presents - Seamus/Front door - Doyle
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: Sometime around ten, someone or other will lock it. Stops it getting blown open, if nothing else.
