conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Ruairí - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: Well! I'm a local to the area, and I mostly practice here, but I trained in Dublin. I still find reason to travel there, now and then.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Ruairí - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: As for my... less strictly scientific interests, there has long been a tradition of folk magic in Ireland.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Ruairí - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: Situation depending, of course. Not everyone takes kindly to magic. But then again, not everyone takes kindly to medicine.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Ruairí - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: So these days, I practice my own brand of magic and medicine as something of a dual craft.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Carmela - Ruairí
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you met Miss Mantovani?

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Carmela - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: You know, I have. I've been fortunate enough to spend some time with her.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Carmela - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: I'd never had the pleasure before this event, but I've found conversation with her to be intriguing. She has some fascinating insights into our work here.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Carmela - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: It's a shame she's only in this part of the world every now and then.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Fiadh - Ruairí
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What can you tell me about Miss Callaghan?

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Fiadh - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: Fiadh is my aunt on my father's side, and she's been teaching me in the old ways almost as long as I can remember.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Fiadh - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: I wasn't the only one of her nieces and nephews she gave instruction to, of course, but I was the best at it, and had the determination to follow it.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Fiadh - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: I have been her... apprentice nearly all my life. She's a very talented woman, with a rightful place of honour in the community - their Bean Draoí.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Fiadh - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: Stubborn as a mule and occasionally hot-headed, to be sure, but we can't be all virtue, I suppose.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Fiadh - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: I've been warding thresholds, scrying in wells, and charming work tools since I could read and write.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Sinnott - Ruairí
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you spoken with Father Sinnott?

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Sinnott - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: I... don't have a lot to discuss with priests. They tend to find my approach to things to be... unorthodox.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Sinnott - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: I am surprised to see a man of the cloth at the event. I do not buy his "just keeping an eye on things" line, not for one moment.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Arwa - Ruairí
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you met Miss Hisham?

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Arwa - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: I have, as it happens. She's a fascinating woman, and incredibly sharp.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Arwa - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: Very clued in, too. I think if she could focus, she would make a great leader for her people. Lord knows they'll need people like her in the coming years.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Arwa - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: But right now, she has that way about her - the kind that people get when they are a little... too lost in the magical side of things.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Arwa - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: Which is strange as she is no magician and not really into all that. Maybe she's just caught up in the atmosphere of the séance?

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Saoirse - Ruairí
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Have you met the cook, Miss Murphy?

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Saoirse - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: Only in the loosest of senses, but she was a lot warmer with Fiadh.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Saoirse - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: I've gotten wind she had some visits from one of the local doctors a year or so ago. I never got the details but perhaps her coldness comes from that?

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Blake - Ruairí
speaker: Mister Ward
en: You are from the area, Doctor. Do you know the Marquess at all?

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Blake - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: No, not really. I left for my studies a long time ago, and when I came back, I had no reason to visit this place.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Blake - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: The man I see now, though, bears no resemblance to the vibrant man I recall from my youth.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on O'Finn - Ruairí
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Can you tell me much about Mister Ó Finn?

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on O'Finn - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: Ah yes. Our druid friend. He's alright. His heart's in the right place but his code of conduct is so dated.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on O'Finn - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: He needs to be more open to progress. I think he would achieve more if he were.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Walter Blake - Ruairí
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Were you aware that Marquess Blake has a son?

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Walter Blake - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: He didn't, of course, when I left for my studies. I first heard of the boy after the accident - they needed a doctor to help him with his lingering damages.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Walter Blake - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: Anyway, I received a letter asking me to consider returning home for the task, but nothing came of it. I assume they went with somebody resident to the region.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Walter Blake - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: Probably a blessing, in hindsight. I don't need to travel between here and Dublin any more than I do already.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Walter Blake - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: He was in the carriage, the one that killed his mother, you see. Came out alive but at some cost, I gather.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Walter Blake - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: I've never actually met the Blakes before this event, but I do know of Blake's son. A few years ago, the Marquess was looking for a doctor for him, on account of the accident and its lingering damage.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Character Presents - Ruairí/Opinion on Walter Blake - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: Anyway, I was considered for the task, but I think they chose a local doctor. I heard nothing more after a few back and forths.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Analysis Presents - (to) Ruairí/Scent of antiseptic - Ruairí
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Forgive me for asking, but are your hands okay?

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Analysis Presents - (to) Ruairí/Scent of antiseptic - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: Oh, ha! Yes, they are. I work with chemicals - carbolic acid to sterilized wounds and various others to develop pictures. It has left my hands looking worse for wear, though.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Analysis Presents - (to) Ruairí/Good quality suit - Ruairí
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I was admiring your suit. It looks very well made.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Analysis Presents - (to) Ruairí/Good quality suit - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: It's seen better days, I'm sure, but a local doctor hardly makes enough for a new one at the drop of the hat. Unfortunately.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Analysis Presents - (to) Ruairí/Good quality suit - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: Anyway, thank you. Frankly, I'm concerned I'm underdressed, so I appreciate the compliment.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Analysis Presents - (to) Ruairí/Good quality suit - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: Are you...? Ah, you're being sincere. I see.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Analysis Presents - (to) Ruairí/Celtic cross tie pin - Ruairí
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you often wear that pin?

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Analysis Presents - (to) Ruairí/Celtic cross tie pin - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: Oh? Ah, this. You know, it's habit. Settles patients. I forgot I even had it on.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Analysis Presents - (to) Ruairí/Celtic cross tie pin - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: But I'm not here as a practising doctor, so I can afford it for a few days.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Analysis Presents - (to) Ruairí/Celtic cross tie pin - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: Well, this is Ireland. A strong sense of guilt and shame has been bred into even the freest of us.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Analysis Presents - (to) Ruairí/Celtic cross tie pin - Ruairí
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: I'm a pagan myself, but this is Ireland. A strong sense of guilt and shame has been bred into even the freest of us.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Ruairí's camera
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I've seen one of these before, at a fair. A... camera, I believe?

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Ruairí's camera
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: A good eye, Mister Ward, and only partially wrong.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Ruairí's camera
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: A good eye, Sir, and only partially wrong.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Ruairí's camera
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: It is a camera, yes, but one modified to work as a spirit camera.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Ruairí's camera
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: Well... I modified it to work better as one. Any camera, in the right circumstances, can capture a spirit, of course.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Ruairí's camera
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: But my lens filters the image through complex geometry made of peridot, selenite, black tourmaline, labradorite, lapis lazuli and clear quartz stones to both bring out the spirit and protect against it.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Ruairí's camera
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: I thought, what better place to really put this device to the test than here.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Ruairí's camera
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: These halls and - dare I say, the people here - are likely crawling with spirits.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Ruairí's camera
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: I've even set up a darkroom in my quarters so I can quickly develop images. This way people can take away a copy, should they wish.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Ruairí's camera
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: Would you care for a picture? See who or what haunts you? Aha!

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Ruairí's camera
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ YES ]

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Ruairí's camera
speaker: Detective Ward

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Ruairí's camera
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: Excellent! Come. In my room I have everything needed to take and develop your picture quickly.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Ruairí's camera
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: Of course. It is not for everybody.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Ruairí's camera
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Lead the way.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/camera after ward's image taken
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: There you go. As simple as that.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/camera after ward's image taken
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: Now, if you would care to follow me to my room, I will develop the image for you.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/camera after ward's image taken
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Lead the way.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/camera after ward's image taken
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: Now... Stand still. This will only take a moment.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Ward in room - Ruairi
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: Mister Ward? How exactly did you get into my room?

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Ward in room - Ruairi
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: I promise you, there's nothing in here that would be of value to a common thief.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Ward in room - Ruairi
speaker: Mister Ward
en: A common thief? But-

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Ward in room - Ruairi
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: If you have a better justification, you can give it to the manager.

conversation: Cast/Ruarí Callaghan/Ward in room - Ruairi
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: Sir? How exactly did you get into my room?

conversation: Ground floor/Telegram room/Comments from Ward/Use morse code book on telegram machine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Let's see here...

conversation: Ground floor/Telegram room/Comments from Ward/Use morse code book on telegram machine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: "No communication received Tues 24 from the Manor. Regards."

conversation: Ground floor/Telegram room/Comments from Ward/Use morse code book on telegram machine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: It seems like Miss Deane didn't send for a carriage that night... nor did anyone else, for that matter.

conversation: Ground floor/Telegram room/Comments from Ward/telegram machine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: The hotel's primary means of communication with the outside world.

conversation: Ground floor/Telegram room/Comments from Ward/telegram machine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I could contact the exchange and confirm, I don't know how to send a message with this. It has to be entered in Morse code.

conversation: Ground floor/Telegram room/Comments from Ward/telegram machine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: The staff likely send messages on guests' behalves. One of them must know Morse, or have a guide to help with it...

conversation: Ground floor/Telegram room/Comments from Ward/telegram machine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I wonder if Miss Deane would have used this to call for a ride off the manor grounds?

conversation: Ground floor/Telegram room/Comments from Ward/telegram machine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Perhaps I can use that Morse code guide I have to contact the exchange and ask?

conversation: Ground floor/Telegram room/Comments from Ward/telegram machine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Apparently the battery is dead. It requires 6 Volts.

conversation: Ground floor/Telegram room/Comments from Ward/telegram machine
speaker: Mister Ward
en: It seems to be working now.

conversation: Ground floor/east corridor ground/comments from NPCs/varley dinner door
speaker: Mister Varley
en: Secondly, there will be no staff. We'll be having our own meal in the servants' hall - though, of course, your food has already been prepared.

conversation: Ground floor/east corridor ground/comments from NPCs/varley dinner door
speaker: Mister Varley
en: Mister Ward. Will you be joining the silent dinner?

conversation: Ground floor/east corridor ground/comments from NPCs/varley dinner door
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I am. In fact, the Marquess has invited me to join him for a meal.

conversation: Ground floor/east corridor ground/comments from NPCs/varley dinner door
speaker: Mister Varley
en: I am sorry, Sir. Guests need to be seated by half past the hour in order to dine.

conversation: Ground floor/east corridor ground/comments from NPCs/varley dinner door
speaker: Mister Varley
en: Can I help you with anything else?

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/basement door
speaker: Mister Ward
en: The staff area is locked off.

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/basement door
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I can't get inside. I'll try other avenues and come back here if they go nowhere.

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/wall opening sound
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What in God's name was that?

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/wall opening sound
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What is-?

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/painting analysis/blake painting with glyph
speaker: Mister Ward
en: "Percival Blake, the fourth Marquess of Doon."

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/painting analysis/blake painting with glyph
speaker: Mister Ward
en: A nasty looking character, for sure...

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/painting analysis/missing eye
speaker: Mister Ward
en: It's a shame that whatever left him with this wound didn't kill him.

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/painting analysis/present eye
speaker: Mister Ward
en: It is just me or is his remaining eye looking downwards?

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/painting analysis/tassels
speaker: Mister Ward
en: The buttons on his jacket have the same pattern as those on the missing doorway at Room 15.

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/painting analysis/tassels
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What an unusual layout of buttons.

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/painting analysis/tassels
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What an unusual pattern used to tie his coat.

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/painting analysis/sun door
speaker: Mister Ward
en: A distinct archway. I do not recall seeing it in the hotel yet.

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/painting analysis/sun door
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I've seen this symbol - it was on an archway just below here.

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/Completing quest
speaker: Mister Ward
en: How long were they trapped here?

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/Completing quest
speaker: Mister Ward
en: How long can a soul linger, and why?

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/Completing quest
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I wonder... Eamonn… No, best not dwell on it.

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/see sun door
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What's this? Another pattern like in the dream?

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/see sun door
speaker: Mister Ward
en: This one looks like the pattern where the door to Room 15 should be.

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/see sun door
speaker: Mister Ward
en: It has the same sun motif above it as was on the painting upstairs.

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/complete first glyph
speaker: Mister Ward
en: It's... there's a door hidden behind this wall!

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/complete first glyph
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Am I... Am I still dreaming?

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/complete first glyph
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I don't... How is this possible? What is this place?

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/room 1/bucket in room 1
speaker: Mister Ward
en: It looks clean - possibly held water?

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/room 1/seeing room 1
speaker: Mister Ward
en: The air is rotted here…

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/room 1/seeing room 1
speaker: Mister Ward
en: This is an unholy place...

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/room 1/remains room 1
speaker: Mister Ward
en: These look like... bones. This skull… it appears to be huma-

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/room 1/remains room 1
speaker: Mister Ward
en: These... must have belonged to that woman...

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/room 1/remains room 1
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I hope they have found peace.

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/room 1/remains room 1
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Her spirit, her soul, seems bound to these bones... And not by choice...

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/room 1/remains room 1
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What earthly power could do such a thing?

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/room 1/used manacles
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I can see brown stains on them that suggests they were used...

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/room 1/other manacles
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Thankfully I can't tell if these ever saw use.

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/room 1/crud
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I don't want to think about what these stains were...

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/room 1/after seeing ghost 1
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I don't want to think about what these stains were...

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/room 1/after ghosts depart
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Percival damned them to an eternity of torment. And for what?

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/room 1/after ghosts depart
speaker: Mister Ward
en: He knew their screams would go unheard.

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/room 1/after ghosts depart
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I pray they find the peace they deserve…

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/room 1/after ghosts depart
speaker: Mister Ward
en: May God have mercy on their souls.

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/on start after ghost room 1
speaker: Mister Ward
en: That hole wasn't there before...

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/room 2/remains room 2
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Another skeleton in pieces... Is this what she wanted me to find?

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/room 2/see room 2
speaker: Mister Ward
en: This space is even worse than the first one...

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/room 2/see door 2
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Another sigil back here. Somebody must have sealed off the passage to this area sometime after Percival walled it up.

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/seen ghost
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Was that a... No, it couldn't have been.

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/seen ghost
speaker: Mister Ward
en: My eyes are deceiving me. A hallucination caused by gas or mould in the air perhaps?

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/seen ghost
speaker: Mister Ward
en: ...but then, how can I explain these flames?

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south east/etienne placation
speaker: Mister Ward
en: This seems important. I should come back to this once I have placated Mister Toussaint's demands.

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south west/basement door
speaker: Mister Ward
en: The door is locked.

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south west/basement door
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I would need a key to progress. With some luck the same would have been true for Miss Deane.

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south west/basement door
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I'll look elsewhere and come back if needs be.

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south west/knocked painting
speaker: Mister Ward
en: The painting is off balance.

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south west/knocked painting
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Miss Deane, perhaps?

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south west/knocked painting
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Likely knocked out of place by Miss Deane when leaving the building.

conversation: Ground floor/towers/south west/knocked painting
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Did somebody pass this way?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Eavesdrop, Ruairí and Fiadh
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: ...Well, then, what do you make of it? And don't just say you don't like it.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Eavesdrop, Ruairí and Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: But I don't! Really, what's more to be said about it? They're kicking up dust they don't even notice, and leaving us to clean up!

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Eavesdrop, Ruairí and Fiadh
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: Still, it's not malicious, aintín. This is... You and I both know there's no better place for a séance like this than here.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Eavesdrop, Ruairí and Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Better they not hold the blasted séance at all! What's it all for, in the end? For the spectacle? You're much too forgiving, Ruairí.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Eavesdrop, Ruairí and Fiadh
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: And somewhere on the other side of forgiving is stubborn.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Eavesdrop, Ruairí and Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: You're not the first person to call me that, you know, and you won't be the last. There is no good to come of this.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Eavesdrop, Ruairí and Fiadh
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: If there were, you wouldn't know it.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Eavesdrop, Ruairí and Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Come on, now, Ruairí...

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Eavesdrop, Ruairí and Fiadh
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: Leave it for once, won't you? I won't be lectured by a woman who won't listen herself.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Mister Dupré
en: If you're looking for a seat, you're welcome to join us. I'm sure my companion here won't mind?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Missus D'Arcy
en: Why not? I'm being educated on the specifics of tomorrow evening's séance, and why, apparently, it's so impressive.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ EXCUSE SELF FROM MEAL ]

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ JOIN THEM ]

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I'm sorry, I haven't the time to stay. Do excuse me.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ TAKE KEY ]

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ LEAVE KEY ]

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Missus D'Arcy
en: What a ruckus...

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Mister Dupré
en: That poor woman... Anyway, where was I? Ah yes...

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Missus D'Arcy
en: All séances are used to speak to ghosts. Is that not the entire point of them?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Missus D'Arcy
en: So, wherein lies the distinction? Surely, if Miss Mantovani has held a séance before, then she has also made a ghost talk before?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Mister Dupré
en: No, though I understand the confusion. We have gotten close to that feat, parallel to it - but direct communication has not been achieved.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Mister Dupré
en: Séances are used to invite a ghost to communicate, and to provide a means for them to do so. In the most successful cases, the spirit speaks through the medium themselves.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Mister Dupré
en: Miss Mantovani intends to--

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Missus D'Arcy
en: Is that really possible?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Mister Dupré
en: Spirits aren't to be trifled with. That gets forgotten, sometimes.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ ASK ABOUT DANGER ]

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ DON'T INTERRUPT ]

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Do you think we'll be in danger attending the séance?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Mister Dupré
en: I am putting my trust in Miss Mantovani. I don't believe she'll lead us wrong.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Mister Dupré
en: We'll be fine, I think, so long as no one disturbs her workings.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Missus D'Arcy
en: But no one has ever truly been hurt by a spirit, as I hear it. When that has happened, it's been proven to be the work of charlatans; their tools getting out of hand. Isn't that right?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Mister Dupré
en: While it isn't common, I'm afraid that's not exactly true, my dear. I've seen it myself. Provoked spirits can be dangerous.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Missus D'Arcy
en: ...Perhaps I'll stand farther back from the proceedings than I initially planned.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Missus D'Arcy
en: But I don't think I'm done with my questions, Mister Dupré. I want to know more about your practice.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Mister Dupré
en: It would be my pleasure.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Missus D'Arcy
en: After breakfast, would you join me for some air out front?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Mister Dupré
en: Of course.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Missus D'Arcy
en: Would you believe that he's somewhat of an expert on all things related to death?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Declan Ward. Pleased to meet you both.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Missus D'Arcy
en: More than that, evidently! We were just talking about this "Grand Séance" and I'm trying to understand what it is that makes it so grand.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Mister Dupré
en: She means I am an undertaker.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Mister Dupré
en: Allow me to introduce Missus Olivia D'Arcy. And I am Lloyd Dupré.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Missus D'Arcy
en: Aaah!

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Missus Joyce
en: Oh dear... I've made a right hames of this... Don't fret, nothing's broke.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Mister Dupré
en: Do you need help, Missus Joyce?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Missus Joyce
en: Oh no, Sir, thank you. I managed to drop it, I can manage to pick it back up, I'm sure.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Mister Dupré
en: But those cases are debunked at worst and uncorroborated at best - there is no way to prove, beyond doubt, the medium did not make it up.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Mister Dupré
en: Now. In any records of direct sightings - and this is true of my own... encounters - the ghosts do not, can not, speak for themselves.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Missus D'Arcy
en: But, I could have sworn I'd left my key here...? Maybe I dropped it?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Missus D'Arcy
en: Oh, my key. I should put that back in my purse before I forget it.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Missus D'Arcy
en: I'm sorry, Mister Dupré - we will have to postpone that conversation. Once we're finished here, I'll need to go to reception and ask whether anyone has turned in my key.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Mister Dupré
en: The hope is that Miss Mantovani, with the right time, place, and people around her, will cut out the middleman - or middlewoman in this case - and have the spirit speak for itself!

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Mister Dupré
en: Tomorrow night, the veil between worlds will be at its thinnest. And it's especially thin here, in this part of the country.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Mister Dupré
en: Then the hotel... it's not without its storied history. Plenty of uncrossed souls in these walls.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Mister Dupré
en: That, of course, is where the danger lies...

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Missus D'Arcy
en: Danger?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Mister Dupré
en: Of course, Madam. I'll be in the courtyard, should you find time to join me.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Dupre and D'arcy
speaker: Mister Dupré
en: To the courtyard, then, Missus D'Arcy.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: Care to join us, Sir? If you don't mind me speaking for you both, of course?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Mister O'Meara
en: No, it's alright. Maybe he knows something about Miss Hisham's friend?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ EXCUSE SELF FROM MEAL ]

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ JOIN THEM ]

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Mister Ward
en: You're very kind, but I don't have the time, just now. Thank you, all the same.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Please. Declan Ward, thank you for letting me join.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Miss Hisham
en: Miss Deane. Evelyn Deane. Have you met her?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Mister O'Meara
en: Yeah, okay. Now, Miss Hisham, who is your friend?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Mister O'Meara

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Mister O'Meara
en: Is this a joke? Did Eve... Miss Deane put you up to this?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Miss Hisham
en: I don't...

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: Mister O'Meara! Please!

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Mister O'Meara
en: Sorry, sorry. Yes, I know Miss Deane. We have... history...

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: Hmpf. What about her, Miss Hisham?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Miss Hisham
en: Thank you. I was meant to meet her yesterday. Or the day before? It's... cloudy.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Miss Hisham
en: But I haven't seen her. And I asked the staff, and, after blank stares, I was told she had left.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Mister O'Meara
en: She left? That doesn't seem correct. Why would she go? She lives for this stuff!

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: A family matter, maybe?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ ADMIT KNOWING HER FATHER ]

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ ADMIT YOU NEVER MET HER ]

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Miss Hisham
en: Do you know her, Sir?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: As much as I know any of you three, I'm afraid. We talked at the afternoon tea on Tuesday - which turned into afternoon drinks, which turned into my needing a slow start on Wednesday.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Mister O'Meara
en: I thought maybe she sent you down here to make fun at my expense. It would be the sort of thing she would find amusing.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Mister O'Meara
en: Tuesday, you say?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Miss Hisham
en: You, Mister Ward? Do you know her?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I have had... dealings with her father.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Mister O'Meara
en: With Rupert? You must be a shady devil then, Mister Ward!

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Mister Ward
en: No. I only arrived yesterday. If she has left, then I've missed my chance to meet her.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Miss Hisham
en: Hmm. Very well. I hope she is okay. I overheard that the telegraph machine is recovered. I'll send something to her home, so she can contact me on her return.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Mister O'Meara
en: Ha, I'm only making fun. Mister Deane is a... hardfisted businessman. Certainly, I doubt you know him from church.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Miss Hisham
en: Please excuse me.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: Of course. I'll take this opportunity to make my leave, as well.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Mister Ward
en: You are correct there, Mister O'Meara. I don't know much about his daughter - does the apple fall far from the tree?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Mister Ward
en: ...I'm sorry that I cannot help you, Miss Hisham, but I'll keep an eye out.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Mister O'Meara
en: Me too. This whole meal has left me painfully upset.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: Of course. I'll take this opportunity to make my leave, as well.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Mister O'Meara
en: Ohhh...

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Mister O'Meara
en: Yes and no, I suppose. She certainly has his drive and forceful personality. And disdain for the Man Upstairs.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Mister O'Meara
en: But she is less interested in material things than he.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: It is very easy to not care about material things when you have so much of them to hand.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 2 - Cathal and Arwa
speaker: Mister O'Meara

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: I understand the concern, Signorina, I do... Oh, but - Mister Ward, would you like to join us?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: We were just talking about... well, whether this séance is such a good idea. You're welcome to join us, if you like.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ EXCUSE SELF FROM MEAL ]

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ JOIN THEM ]

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I wish I could, but I don't have the time just now. Please excuse me.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I'd be delighted to. Is there doubt about the séance?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Consider yourself excused.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: Sì, Signorina Callaghan has concerns about it taking place.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: If you ask me, Mister Ward, there's nothing good to come of this. Best to leave these lands be. They're unsettled enough already...

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: But it is one spirit, mio amica, among many, apprehended for less than an hour. If I thought it would cause much trouble, I would not do it.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: And it is the Marquess' home. Surely he would not invite me to do such a thing if it would cause trouble in his ancestral home.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Hmph. I'm not sure the Marquess knows what's good for him.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ ASK MISS CALLAGHAN'S REASONING ]

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ ASK ABOUT MISS MANTOVANI'S INVITATION ]

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What is it that has you so concerned, Miss Callaghan?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Ah... See, this was once sacred ground. There are portals - ways to the Otherworld, underground all over the country. But this place housed a significant one.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I worry that when our medium here calls forth something from the other side, she'll call the wrong thing...

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: Tsk! You offend me - I am a better medium than that! *cough* *cough*

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: You'll call out in a place you don't know where things you don't know walk. They are tricksters - they can call back in any way that pleases you!

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Am I right to assume that Marquess Blake invited you here himself?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: Yes. He contacted me directly and insisted I host his séance.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: He said he had heard of my ability and could settle for no less. - how could I refuse that, Signor?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: That is... strange, I must admit, but I do not find I can refuse. And besides, everything I know about séances...

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: Even with what we are planning, there is nothing to suggest there will be trouble.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: I understand the concern, Signorina, I do... Ah, but - this man would like to join us, yes?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: You know my thoughts on it.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: I will do my best for you, Signorina, I promise.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Well... Ah, that more people were as reasonable. Thank you for that, at least, Miss Mantovani.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: Please, my name is Carmela.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: Excuse my interrupting... but I have to wonder. If what Miss Callaghan says is true, and there is a gateway here, and this séance is the first of its sort...

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: I think that would suggest then, if something unexpected were to happen, it could well happen here. Is that not so?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: I suppose that is true.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Exactly! This entire event is meddling in factors we cannot - even those of us who know the land - know the outcome of.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: Which would make for a fascinating revelation, would it not, Miss Callaghan?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Oh, for pity's sake...

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: I could say, amica mia, that it is only one spirit. One among many, apprehended for less than an hour.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: Were it to cause much trouble-- *cough* I would not do it.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: This is, of course, a lie!

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: How can I say it is safe when it has not been done before? Of course, I would risk this!

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: And the Marquess, he sees value in that risk, too.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I worry that when our medium here calls forth something from the other side, she'll put something askew we can't put right again.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: How could I refuse that, Signor? He has never told me the specifics as to why he requires it... he avoided the question when I asked.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Were you the only invited guest?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: Signor! You offend me! I am the main event, no? Am I not enough for you?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: I got no invite.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: Haha, and now I understand why!

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: How can you know 'til it's done?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: And right now, you seem most eager to succeed at any cost!

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: Excuse my interrupting... a portal... underground?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: As such, aye.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: Do you know a way to it?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Oh. That's long lost, since the invasions.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Not that I'd tell a man of God, even if it wasn't. Hasn't your kind plundered our myths enough?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: Mmmm...

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Dinner day 2 - Carmella, Sinnott, Fiadh
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: I do not know? Perhaps they were invited, or perhaps my reputation precedes me! *cough*

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Ah, you would be... Mister Ward? Thank you for accepting my invitation.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ EXCUSE SELF FROM MEAL ]

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ JOIN HIM ]

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I'm afraid I cannot. Please excuse me, Marquess.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Ah, Mister Ward. Good to speak with you again. I trust you are enjoying your time with us here at the manor?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: You will join me for lunch, then?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Yes, thank you for the offer.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I will admit, it is not often that I get to dine with nobility.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: What brought you here, Mister Ward?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I beg your pardon?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Are you a student of the occult? You are a working man, so I do not think you are here to climb social ladders?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Perhaps you... lost... somebody?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ EVELYN DEANE ]

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ BROTHER ]

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ THE TENANTS ]

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ STAY SILENT ]

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I lost my... brother. Eamonn.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: We were firemen.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I came here looking for Evelyn Deane.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Deane? Ah, yes, the departed girl. You must have been disappointed to find her gone when you arrived.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: You are one of the throng of men who seemed to be chasing her.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: She sounds like a fascinating woman. I wish I'd been able to meet her.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Were?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I stopped. After a blaze took him.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I know fishermen who think that when the sea takes them, it's their time to go.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I never met a fireman who felt the same about flames.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I am sorry for your loss.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: My wife... She... died in a carriage accident. Same one that crippled our boy.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Me too.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I lost my wife. She... died in a carriage accident. Same one that crippled our boy...

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: A loss it is, then.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: It's okay. I know it can be hard to speak on these things.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Do you know there were reports of over one hundred different ghosts wandering these grounds?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: After it happened, I would wheel Walter around night after night, hoping to see her.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Eventually... he asked to stop coming.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Maybe 'gave up' is being unfair on myself, given this event.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: In another life, I was a fireman.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: But not her.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: The silent dinner, Mister Ward. Will you invite your brother to it?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Well, I hope that whatever solace you seek here, you find it.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ YES ]

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Detective Ward

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I... think I will, yes.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: ...No. I have made my peace with what happened to him. He's best left resting in the past.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I shall have the housekeeper lay a place out for him, then. It is at 8pm sharp this evening. You would not want to miss him, should he come.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I wish I had your wisdom and your resolve, Mister Ward.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I also hope you are wrong and that I am right to try to speak with her again. We shall see, as they say.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Now. If you will excuse me, there is a lot to prepare for later on. Good day, Mister Ward.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: There were lives lost along the way.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Inevitable in that work. Inevitable in the conditions people are forced to live in, work in.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: But one... one fire, I cannot let go.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I carry those lives with me still. Perhaps forever.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I am sorry for your loss, though I am sure you saved more lives than slipped through your fingers.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Mister Ward
en: That is probably true. But I had to leave the job after that. I couldn't face the flames without seeing them. And it is not a role that forgives hesitation.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I imagine not. I...

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Not long after that, I gave up, too.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I have somehow convinced myself that if all this is true - this business with the séance, maybe I can see her again. Speak with her... again...

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I am the Marquess of Doon, Jonathan Blake. We haven't had much chance to speak since you arrived.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Lunch day 3 - Blake
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: A shame. I had hoped to sit with all the guests before the séance, but I cannot force you to join me.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Comments from Ward/Plant

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Comments from Ward/Plant 2

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Comments from Ward/Suit of armour
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Another suit of armour.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Comments from Ward/Suit of armour 2

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Comments from Ward/Plants on table
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Better these be in here than outside, with the weather the way it is.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Comments from Ward/Dumbwaiter
speaker: Mister Ward
en: This will be how they get the food from the kitchen so quickly.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Comments from Ward/Dumbwaiter

en: It is too small to transport anything larger than a covered platter.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Comments from Ward/Hearthfire
speaker: Mister Ward
en: There must be three dozen fireplaces in this place, and I'm grateful for every one of them.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Comments from Ward/Crockery
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Best I leave this alone, I think.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Eavesdrop, Coventry and Caitlin

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Eavesdrop, Coventry and Caitlin

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Eavesdrop, Coventry and Caitlin
speaker: Missus Joyce
en: I've not the faintest, but I noticed that it's finally gone down.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Eavesdrop, Coventry and Caitlin
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: Has it now?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Eavesdrop, Coventry and Caitlin
speaker: Missus Joyce
en: Aye, Sir. It's been climbing all week but finally went the other way this morning.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Eavesdrop, Coventry and Caitlin
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: How odd. I wonder what caused that?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/silent dinner
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I... suppose I shouldn't stare... Varley said it upsets them...

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/silent dinner
speaker: Mister Ward
en: There is a key here?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/silent dinner
speaker: Mister Ward
en: The note reads "Blake Residence. Now."

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/silent dinner
speaker: Mister Ward
en: What's this?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/silent dinner
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Then, I suppose, all there is to do is eat...

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/silent dinner
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Who is that? And why is she facing away?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/silent dinner
speaker: Mister Ward
en: ...Eamonn?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/silent dinner
speaker: Mister Ward
en: ...Ghosts...

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/silent dinner
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Where did this come from? Did my secret employer manage to get this to me? But who are they?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/silent dinner
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Missus Joyce, I assume.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/silent dinner
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Lord save me, I cannot get used to this...

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/silent dinner
speaker: Mister Ward
en: The ghost from the hedge maze!

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/silent dinner
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Laura? She returned for this - despite being freed...

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/silent dinner
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Is that Mary Blake? Why is she facing away?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/silent dinner
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Missus Lau's husband...

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/silent dinner
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Alexander Quinn?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/silent dinner
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I did not think... that you could actually... could actually...

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/silent dinner
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Perhaps it's a good time to investigate, since the Marquess and most of the guests appear to be here...

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/silent dinner
speaker: Mister Ward

en: A moment, Mister Ward?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Cathal catches you in a lie
speaker: Mister O'Meara
en: Unless I am mistaken, you told me earlier that you knew Evelyn?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Cathal catches you in a lie
speaker: Mister O'Meara
en: Whereas just now you've claimed not to know her at all?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Cathal catches you in a lie

en: So... which is it?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Cathal catches you in a lie
speaker: Mister Ward

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Cathal catches you in a lie
speaker: Mister O'Meara
en: Her leaving does seem suspicious. She loves these things.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Cathal catches you in a lie
speaker: Mister O'Meara
en: ...as I mentioned, she was out of it when I saw her. I'd said she was at the bar - and that is likely true.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Cathal catches you in a lie
speaker: Mister O'Meara
en: But she may well have been there getting something from the barman, the porter - Doyle.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Cathal catches you in a lie
speaker: Mister O'Meara
en: He's a bit of a user, and Evelyn always finds those. Anyone with a supply can share a supply.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Cathal catches you in a lie
speaker: Mister O'Meara
en: Maybe you can learn something from him?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Cathal catches you in a lie
speaker: Mister Ward
en: I've already talked to him and he was a great help. Thank you.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Cathal catches you in a lie
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Thank you, that is useful information to have.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/silent dinner redo

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/silent dinner redo

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/silent dinner redo

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/silent dinner redo

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/silent dinner redo
speaker: Mister Ward

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/silent dinner redo

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/silent dinner redo

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/silent dinner redo
speaker: Mister Ward

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/silent dinner redo
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Mary Blake?

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/silent dinner redo
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Her gaze is cutting across my tray.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/silent dinner redo
speaker: Mister Ward
en: If so, then I won't waste it.

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/silent dinner redo
speaker: Mister Ward

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/silent dinner redo

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Etienne tattles

conversation: Ground floor/Dining room/Breakfast day 2 - Etienne tattles

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Mister Toussaint
en: And these fae--

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: --please, Sir, call them 'The Other Crowd', 'Other Folk', or similar unless you want to draw their eye to this place.

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Mister Toussaint
en: My apologies, Madame. These Other Folk, they differ from the winged fairies of children's stories, oui?

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: As much as you and I differ from a wild animal, yes.

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: There are several distinct groups of people that must be considered when talking about Irish mythology.

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Mister Skerritt
en: Thank you, Marquess. Not to turn things gruesome, but is it true? What do they say about the walled-up rooms?

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Marquess Blake

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Certainly, it is said that Percival Blake bricked away people who crossed him, but no proof was ever found.

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Spending too much time digging around in our library, eh Mister Skerritt?

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Unless he magicked the evidence away, I think we can lay these rumours to rest.

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: In the First Cycle, there are the Tuatha De Danann, a race of god-like entities.

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: The stories of the Second Cycle are primarily concerned with the ancient kingdoms that once made up the land.

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: The Third Cycle centres around the exploits of hunters and bards, led by the hero Fionn Mac Cumhaill.

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: And finally, there is the fourth cycle - the Cycle of Kings. The fourth cycle is also that in which we find the story of the Milesians, our forefathers.

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: These are the people who would win a battle against the Tuatha Dé Danann, and consign them to the Otherworld.

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Mister Dupré
en: It is my opinion that characters of gods hold particular sway across the world if they have a domain that is common to the human experience.

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Mister Dupré
en: And while we no longer live in an age of warriors and great battles, such as that the Mórrigan was said to oversee…

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Mister Dupré
en: Bríd, goddess of poets, would surely still have domain with the authors of our age...

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Mister Dupré
en: And one must imagine the spirit of Giobniu would be found in the Industrial Revolution that makes so much possible.

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Mister Dupré
en: The domains of gods are not lost, not to those that would worship them. They simply change.

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Mister Dupré
en: Across time and continents, their domains still hold meaning even if they take forms we no longer recognise. Such is the nature of things.

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: The body of Christ.

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Miss Murphy

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Miss Murphy

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: ... Does something trouble you, my child?

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: By their nature, they are hard to define. And yet, even in their... elusive... ness... Questo funzionerà... we find them everywhere.

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: By their many names, they are all across the world. There are many formations...

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: Some echo the grief they left upon the world and are blind to the living. *cough*

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: While others are vengeful and aggressive.

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: Regardless. No single spectre experienced has been able to directly communicate.

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: But tomorrow night - ah tomorrow night we intend to change this!

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: So, I am sure you all know this land came into the Blake family in the 1650s after Cromwell's invasion.

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: What I found interesting was what came before...

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: This land was a place of worship and innovation.

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: A gathering spot for scholars and engineers, and artists to work on understanding and advancement - the betterment of their people.

conversation: Ground floor/West Corridor Ground/drawing room eavesdrop
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: Easy pickings for Edward Blake. No doubt he and Cromwell cared very little for any knowledge held by 'primitive pagans'...

conversation: Ground floor/Library/comments from Ward/Bookshelves/1 - Blake history
speaker: Mister Ward
en: "Edward Blake, 1630-1703, was an Englishman serving in the Cromwellian conquest of Ireland by the (then) English Commonwealth."

conversation: Ground floor/Library/comments from Ward/Bookshelves/1 - Blake history
speaker: Detective Ward
en: Look up the Blake Family.

conversation: Ground floor/Library/comments from Ward/Bookshelves/1 - Blake history
speaker: Mister Ward
en: "Originally of the English Blakes, the branch of the family now resident in Ireland’s Connacht region..."

conversation: Ground floor/Library/comments from Ward/Bookshelves/1 - Blake history
speaker: Mister Ward
en: "...are descendants of the illustrious war veteran Edward Blake, who served during the Cromwellian conquest of Ireland."

conversation: Ground floor/Library/comments from Ward/Bookshelves/1 - Blake history
speaker: Mister Ward
en: "In reward for his service and valour, Blake was rewarded some of the seized land, on which he built the manor now known as Blake Manor."

conversation: Ground floor/Library/comments from Ward/Bookshelves/1 - Blake history
speaker: Mister Ward
en: "While there are, it must be admitted, a number of ghoulish tales about Edward Blake and his subsequent family line..."

conversation: Ground floor/Library/comments from Ward/Bookshelves/1 - Blake history
speaker: Mister Ward
en: "...these should not be paid heed – for surely they indicate nothing more than superstition and occasional local unrest."

conversation: Ground floor/Library/comments from Ward/Bookshelves/1 - Blake history
speaker: Mister Ward
en: "He was a notable figure among the English forces, and was credited for his success by Cromwell himself, who awarded him a significant parcel of conquered land in Connacht."

conversation: Ground floor/Library/comments from Ward/Bookshelves/1 - Blake history
speaker: Mister Ward
en: "The Blakes have gone on to become significant figureheads in their community, and have upheld their position for a few hundred years."

conversation: Ground floor/Library/comments from Ward/Bookshelves/1 - Blake history
speaker: Detective Ward
en: Look up Wilhelmina Blake.

conversation: Ground floor/Library/comments from Ward/Bookshelves/1 - Blake history
speaker: Mister Ward
en: “The title was passed down to him by Richard Blake, son of William Blake.”

conversation: Ground floor/Library/comments from Ward/Bookshelves/1 - Blake history
speaker: Mister Ward
en: “Richard Blake’s was considered quite the opposite. His interests kept him from the manor, and a few years after his passing in Paris, Jonathan Blake opened the grounds as a hotel to help revitalise the lands post-famine.”

conversation: Ground floor/Library/comments from Ward/Bookshelves/1 - Blake history
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Not much else is recorded about him, he does not seem to have undertaken many other exploits.

conversation: Ground floor/Library/comments from Ward/Bookshelves/1 - Blake history
speaker: Mister Ward

conversation: Ground floor/Library/comments from Ward/Bookshelves/1 - Blake history

conversation: Ground floor/Library/comments from Ward/Bookshelves/1 - Blake history

speaker: Mister Ward

conversation: Ground floor/Library/comments from Ward/Bookshelves/4 - Flora and Fauna

en: "Typically, crows are understood to be black, with long, pointed beaks suitable for scavenging - as they are, indeed, carrion birds."

conversation: Ground floor/Library/comments from Ward/Bookshelves/4 - Flora and Fauna

en: "Carrion birds live off dead flesh, and are abundant as crows in Northern Europe."

conversation: Ground floor/Library/comments from Ward/Bookshelves/5 - Medicine
