speaker: Mister Ward
en: The third light is gone now, too. What thresholds do the lights measure?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/comments from ward/first device drop
speaker: Mister Ward
en: That's all the lights out. What does that mean for the séance, I wonder?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/comments from ward/ward after carmela flyer cutscene
speaker: Mister Ward
en: ...Her? Who could she be talking about? And what does that bible verse mean?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/comments from ward/ward after carmela flyer cutscene
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Clearly, someone in this hotel has bad blood with Miss Mantovani. She thinks it's a woman - could it even be Miss Deane?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/comments from ward/ward after carmela flyer cutscene
speaker: Mister Ward
en: And that knife... Something tells me they're not likely to stop at threats.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/comments from ward/Eti Catches You
speaker: Mister Toussaint
en: ...Wandering into people's rooms like a wayward child is going to get you into trouble, Monsieur Ward.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/comments from ward/Eti Catches You
speaker: Mister Ward
en: That is rich, all things considered.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/comments from ward/Eti Catches You
speaker: Mister Toussaint
en: Ah, but I do not care whose room you break into, Monsieur - as long as it is not mine.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/comments from ward/Eti kicks you out
speaker: Mister Toussaint
en: Monsieur Ward... I warned you. You know what must come next, Oui?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/comments from ward/Eti kicks you out
speaker: Mister Ward
en: ...You're serious, aren't you? Isn't this just a bit hypocritical?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/comments from ward/Eti kicks you out
speaker: Mister Toussaint
en: Come now. Let us go inform the manager of your good work among his guests...

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/comments from ward/Eti kicks you out
speaker: Mister Toussaint
en: Perhaps. But, more importantly, it is sensible.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Eavesdrop conversation, Ivy and Lan Fen
speaker: Miss McLeod
en: Does all this not bore you?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Eavesdrop conversation, Ivy and Lan Fen
speaker: Missus Lau
en: Should it? It's fascinating, in a way. Lots of case studies, certainly.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Eavesdrop conversation, Ivy and Lan Fen
speaker: Miss McLeod
en: It's nothing like your usual sort of thing...

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Eavesdrop conversation, Ivy and Lan Fen
speaker: Missus Lau
en: Oh, it's not at all scientific, but... Look, you're talking to a woman with a shrine in her room. I'm not entirely clinical.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Eavesdrop conversation, Ivy and Lan Fen
speaker: Missus Lau
en: Besides - look at you! Ivy, I said I would come with you! Do you expect me to regret it?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Eavesdrop conversation, Ivy and Lan Fen
speaker: Miss McLeod
en: I suppose... I just thought, what with how things are...

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Eavesdrop conversation, Ivy and Lan Fen
speaker: Missus Lau
en: You're always the first one to know when my temper's run short. Do you suppose I've managed to hide it from you, of all people?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Eavesdrop conversation, Ivy and Lan Fen
speaker: Missus Lau
en: Besides - you know I would take any excuse to spend my time with you.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Eavesdrop conversation, Ivy and Lan Fen
speaker: Miss McLeod
en: Oh - good grief, but I... you are always so sweet.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Eavesdrop conversation, Ivy and Lan Fen
speaker: Missus Lau
en: ...Don't look away like that. Everything will be alright.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Eavesdrop conversation, Ivy and Lan Fen
speaker: Miss McLeod
en: No, no, I just... Maybe it will. I don't know. Maybe.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/ball intro
speaker: Mister Varley
en: Ah. Mister Ward. Our final attendee.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/ball intro
speaker: Mister Ward
en: My apologies. I was delayed in getting ready.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/ball intro
speaker: Mister Varley
en: Of course, Sir. There is no need to excuse your time to us.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/ball intro
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: You've no idea, Sir!

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/ball intro
speaker: Mister Varley
en: This is, however, a masked ball, Sir. If you have not brought your own, we can provide one.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/ball intro
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Please. I seem to be underdressed.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/ball intro
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: Sorry, Mister Varley, Sir. Not my place.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/ball intro
speaker: Mister Varley
en: Hhhmmm...

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/ball intro
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: Anyways. Here's your mask, Sir, and some champagne for the toast.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/ball intro
speaker: Mister Varley
en: You may go on through, Sir. I'm sure the others are eager for your arrival...

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/ball intro
speaker: Mister Ward
en: My thanks...

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Etienne and Varley
speaker: Mister Toussaint
en: I understand it might not be of academic concern to you, but you must see what allowing her attendance does to the event's credibility.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Etienne and Varley
speaker: Mister Varley
en: I'm not about to turn out a guest based on hearsay, Mister Toussaint.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Etienne and Varley
speaker: Mister Varley
en: I'm afraid whatever issue you have with Missus Erickson, it's between yourself and her. I'm not going to intervene.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Etienne and Varley
speaker: Mister Toussaint
en: You misunderstand; I am not asking you to intervene. I am telling you that she is not what she seems.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Etienne and Varley
speaker: Mister Toussaint
en: And consequently that so long as she is in attendance, the entire event is in question. That can't be acceptable, surely?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Etienne and Varley
speaker: Mister Varley
en: The specifics of the event are not up to me, Mister Toussaint. I just manage the hotel.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Etienne and Varley
speaker: Mister Varley
en: If a guest has paid their way and is not causing trouble, then I have no more to say on the matter.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Etienne and Varley
speaker: Mister Toussaint
en: Oh, for... Fine, fine. I understand.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Etienne and Varley
speaker: Mister Toussaint
en: Good day, Monsieur.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Hazel and O'Finn eavesdrop
speaker: Missus Erickson
en: I suspect there is something to be learned about our fortunes here. If only I could have gotten to it before it was cleaned up...

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Hazel and O'Finn eavesdrop
speaker: Mister Ó Finn
en: Why?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Hazel and O'Finn eavesdrop
speaker: Mister Ó Finn
en: Aye, well, I suppose some folks here have never gutted a bird to read its entrails before.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Hazel and O'Finn eavesdrop
speaker: Missus Erickson
en: Is that... some kind of Irish saying?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Hazel and O'Finn eavesdrop
speaker: Mister Ó Finn
en: No?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Hazel and O'Finn eavesdrop
speaker: Missus Erickson
en:
Oh. Well. 
You'll excuse me then.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Hazel and O'Finn eavesdrop
speaker: Mister Ó Finn
en: No. No use for one. Druidry is an oral tradition, so I never got much into the writing. Ogham has served me grand for my purposes - do you want my chisel?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Hazel and O'Finn eavesdrop
speaker: Missus Erickson
en: Eh... No... I was planning on taking some notes.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Hazel and O'Finn eavesdrop
speaker: Missus Erickson
en: I'm sorry Sir, but do you have a pen I can borrow?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Hazel and O'Finn eavesdrop
speaker: Missus Erickson
en: I want to go downstairs and examine the energy left by that poor bird before breakfast.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Hazel and O'Finn eavesdrop
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Mister Ó Finn doesn't write and I didn't see his name on the sign-in book - he must be the person who marked his name with an X. I'll make a note of that.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Eating heart cutscene
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Missus Erickson, we need to talk.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Eating heart cutscene
speaker: Missus Erickson
en: This had best not be about my personal affairs again. Why don't you do us both a favour, Mister Ward, and stop interfering?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Eating heart cutscene
speaker: Missus Erickson
en: What could you, of all people, possibly have to say to me?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Eating heart cutscene
speaker: Mister Ward
en: That's not a bad point. Perhaps you'll be more interested in what Mister Toussaint has to say.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Eating heart cutscene
speaker: Missus Erickson

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Eating heart cutscene
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Shall we go to your room, then? Or would you rather discuss this in the open?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Eating heart cutscene
speaker: Missus Erickson
en: ...Yes. My room, Sir.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Eating heart cutscene
speaker: Mister Ward
en: So, you've read the notes and understand your situation?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Eating heart cutscene
speaker: Missus Erickson
en: He is right... I'm a damned fool...

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Eating heart cutscene
speaker: Missus Erickson
en: But he wins. I forsake this ritual. And I forsake this séance. I have no want to see others enjoying what I will never have.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Eating heart cutscene
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Whether you face eternal damnation, now, is a point of debate - you have assumed that is linked to this magical nullness you have. You may well be wrong...

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Eating heart cutscene
speaker: Mister Ward
en: But if you do this, then you are locking yourself onto that path.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Eating heart cutscene
speaker: Mister Ward
en: And Mister Toussaint will ensure your remaining days will not be easy - magic or no.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Eating heart cutscene
speaker: Missus Erickson
en: I wanted so much to be special, to have what the others have.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Eating heart cutscene
speaker: Missus Erickson
en: But now you have taken that hope from me. Maybe you will have saved my soul, but even now I think I'd pay that price for a taste of that.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Eating heart cutscene
speaker: Missus Erickson
en: If he wasn't going to rob my chance to use and appreciate it.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Eating heart cutscene
speaker: Missus Erickson
en: I would curse you both if I didn't know there would be no venom in my bite.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Eating heart cutscene
speaker: Missus Erickson
en: I hope they see their ghost and more. So much more.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Carmela and Caitlin eavesdrop
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: Please, Missus Joyce, you must listen! You are clearly in pain today.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Carmela and Caitlin eavesdrop
speaker: Missus Joyce
en: ...No. No, get away from me, witch! I'll not hear it, not from you.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Carmela and Caitlin eavesdrop
speaker: Missus Joyce
en: I said I'll not hear it! Rather my joints suffer the cold than your... your... corruption!

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Carmela and Caitlin eavesdrop
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: What is this corruption of yours?  I simply see you need rest.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Carmela and Caitlin eavesdrop
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: Now, my room is big and grand - and a horror to clean, I am sure. You were there an hour on Friday!

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Carmela and Caitlin eavesdrop
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: That is an hour best spent at rest. It is needed, and I am more than capable.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Carmela and Caitlin eavesdrop
speaker: Missus Joyce
en: I... You... you mean to say that-

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Carmela and Caitlin eavesdrop
speaker: Missus Joyce
en: Why would you... No one's ever...

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Carmela and Caitlin eavesdrop
speaker: Missus Joyce
en: N-No. No! Idle hands make the devil's work. Now please, please, leave me be!

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Carmela and Caitlin eavesdrop
speaker: Missus Joyce
en: Oh no, Miss. I'm fine. Thank you.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Carmela and Caitlin eavesdrop
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: Please, Missus Joyce, I beg of you to listen.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Carmela and Caitlin eavesdrop
speaker: Missus Joyce
en: Please now, Miss Mantovani. I said I am fine.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Carmela and Caitlin eavesdrop
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: But I do not need the cards to see how much you carry. You need rest.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Carmela and Caitlin eavesdrop
speaker: Missus Joyce
en: I said I'll not hear it! I'd rather my joints suffer the cold than your... your... corruption, witch!

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Carmela and Caitlin eavesdrop
speaker: Missus Joyce
en: You're... very kind. But no. This old place won't keep itself and I want everything ready for the séance.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/Carmela and Caitlin eavesdrop
speaker: Missus Joyce
en: You all deserve that.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/doyle and saoirse
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: Have you seen Darragh? He's meant to have been helping me move some supplies into the basement all morning.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/doyle and saoirse
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: But once the delivery arrived he's buggered off somewhere.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/doyle and saoirse
speaker: Miss Murphy
en: Maybe? This event is bringing out all sorts of strange behaviour in people.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/doyle and saoirse
speaker: Miss Murphy
en: I don't... Maybe, the service in the church?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/doyle and saoirse
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: Oh he's holy all of a sudden, is he?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/doyle and saoirse
speaker: Mister Doyle

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/doyle and saoirse
speaker: Miss Murphy
en: Thanks for the concern, Seamus.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/doyle and saoirse
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: Ah whatever. I better get back to the stables. Can't leave the basement door just sitting open like that.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/doyle and saoirse
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: Look. Whatever she got you into, just... be careful.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/varley and caitlin discuss keys
speaker: Mister Varley
en: Do you have the master key for the south east corridor?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/varley and caitlin discuss keys
speaker: Missus Joyce
en: Oh no, Mister Varley. I only had the atrium master key with me today.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/varley and caitlin discuss keys
speaker: Missus Joyce
en: Might Mister Hunter have it?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/varley and caitlin discuss keys
speaker: Mister Varley
en: Thank you, no. One of the guests has lost her key and I was hoping I could use this to get her back in.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/varley and caitlin discuss keys
speaker: Mister Varley
en: No, I was just out in the stables. He has the north west corridor locked away in his safe there.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/varley and caitlin discuss keys
speaker: Mister Varley
en: Mister Doyle's key privileges have been revoked.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/varley and caitlin discuss keys
speaker: Missus Joyce
en: Oh, I forgot he locked the southwest key in the basement storage. Has he not gotten that out yet?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/varley and caitlin discuss keys
speaker: Missus Joyce
en: I don't suppose Mister Doyle had it?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/varley and caitlin discuss keys
speaker: Mister Varley
en: Thank you, no. I'm just doing my weekly audit.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/varley and caitlin discuss keys
speaker: Missus Joyce
en: I can fetch it for you? It's only on the room cart in the supply closet.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/varley and caitlin discuss keys
speaker: Missus Joyce
en: What? What in the heavens was he doing in there?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/varley and caitlin discuss keys
speaker: Mister Varley
en: No. He claims he can't find a way through. But I am telling you what I told Mister Hunter - do not do it for him.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/varley and caitlin discuss keys
speaker: Mister Varley
en: And that is not all - the fool also lost the north east corridor master in... one of the unassigned rooms...

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/varley and caitlin discuss keys
speaker: Mister Varley
en: I do not know, but I doubt it was cleaning. When you have time, perhaps you would see if you can find it. And clean up anything he's done.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/varley and caitlin discuss keys
speaker: Missus Joyce
en: Oh, Mister Varley. I've had it up to here with that boy. I'll get to it as soon as I'm done with my morning chores.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/varley and caitlin discuss keys
speaker: Mister Varley
en: Missus Joyce?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/varley and caitlin discuss keys
speaker: Mister Varley
en: I appreciate that.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/varley and caitlin discuss keys
speaker: Missus Joyce

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/varley and caitlin discuss keys
speaker: Mister Varley
en: I would also appreciate some decorum with Miss Mantovani. She is the Marquess' guest and the host of this séance, which you know is important to the future of this manor.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/varley and caitlin discuss keys
speaker: Mister Varley
en: Once this whole business is done, she and the rest of the guests will be moving on. It is only a few days decency, Missus Joyce.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/after key note
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Useful information to have. I've made a note of it.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/carmela sees flyer
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: Please...

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/carmela sees flyer
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: You think this is the first time I have had scripture nailed to my door?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/carmela sees flyer
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: And Leviticus 20:27?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/carmela sees flyer
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: This is not even original!

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/carmela sees flyer
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: Hah!

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/carmela sees flyer
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: It's her isn't it? Oh, she must be very brave indeed.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/carmela sees flyer
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: So scaaaaary with your knife and your Leviticus-es.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/carmela sees flyer
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: Silly woman. I could read the fortunes in your knocked out teeth! *cough* *cough*

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/carmela sees flyer
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: Ah, but truly. I shall have to talk with her sooner rather than later...

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/carmela sees flyer
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: But for now, I need a moment... to sit. *cough* *cough*

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/Conversations/carmela sees flyer
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: I think I know who did this. I will have to talk with her.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/meet the suspects
speaker: Mister Hunter
en: Hard to say, Miss Hisham. Some of the wood up there needs replacing, so all he had to do was hit the wrong part.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/meet the suspects
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Mister Hunter must be the groundsman.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/meet the suspects
speaker: Mister Ward
en: The stable master and groundsman, Mister Darragh Hunter.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/meet the suspects
speaker: Mister Varley
en: What is happening here, Missus Joyce? Myself and the Marquess were in a meeting with Miss Mantovani...

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/meet the suspects
speaker: Miss Hisham
en: How fast must it have been going to break through like that, Mister Hunter?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/meet the suspects
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Well then, I shouldn't keep Walter waiting any longer. Come, I shall leave the rest of you to it and trust everyone to have a good day.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/meet the suspects
speaker: Missus Joyce
en: Oh Sirs. It were a crow. Poor thing was dead on impact.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/meet the suspects
speaker: Miss Murphy
en: Sorry, Marquess...

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/meet the suspects
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Missus Joyce looks to be the housekeeper.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/meet the suspects
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Caitlin Joyce, the housekeeper.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/meet the suspects
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Miss Murphy must be the cook.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/meet the suspects
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Miss Murphy. The cook.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/meet the suspects
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: What's all this about a dead crow? Would that be a bad omen for anyone travelling today, yes?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/meet the suspects
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Please, Mister Coventry... Ó Finn's being here is bad enough omen!

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/meet the suspects
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: Aunt! Some decorum, please.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/meet the suspects
speaker: Missus Erickson
en: Actually, the cards are more of a... tool, a guide. They reflec--

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/meet the suspects
speaker: Mister Toussaint
en: Is there a need to prove yourself, Missus Erickson? Hmm?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/meet the suspects
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Aunt? Perhaps, then, this is our Ruairí and Fiadh Callaghan?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/meet the suspects
speaker: Mister Ward
en: A French accent. He is likely Mister Toussaint, then.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/meet the suspects
speaker: Missus D'Arcy
en: A bad omen? And it didn't show up in your cards, Missus Erickson? Oh my...

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/meet the suspects
speaker: Mister Skerritt
en: Show some respect! Mister Dupré, can't you keep your woman in line?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/meet the suspects
speaker: Mister Skerritt
en: ...Or is your dynamic the other way around?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/meet the suspects
speaker: Mister Dupré
en: Missus D'Arcy is not my woman, Mister Skerritt, nor am I her man. We are people and belong only to ourselves.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/meet the suspects
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: I know your grasp of the esoteric is rudimentary, Missus D'Arcy, but that is not how the cards work. *cough* *cough*

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/meet the suspects
speaker: Mister Ward
en: By a process of elimination, then, that distracted man must be Cathal O'Meara.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/meet the suspects
speaker: Missus D'Arcy

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/meet the suspects
speaker: Mister Ward
en: The Marquess of Doon, Jonathan Blake. Would the boy in that painting be the master of the house, Walter?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/meet the suspects
speaker: Mister Ó Finn
en: Ha! She's said far worse about me and all of it true. Aye. It's a bad omen, Coventry. No doubt about that!

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/meet the suspects
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Given the attire, he is likely Father Lorcan Sinnott.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/meet the suspects
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Those whispering women - only one matching pair signed in at the same time. A Missus Victoria Lau and a Miss Ivy McLeod.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/meet the suspects
speaker: Miss Murphy
en: I was just coming to get you for young Master Walter, he won't eat alone. The food'll go cold 'fore long.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/meet the suspects
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Miss Murphy?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/meet the suspects
speaker: Missus Joyce
en: But don't you worry, we'll get this cleaned up in no time.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/meet the suspects
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Mister Ó Finn? He wasn't in the sign-in book. He must be the 'X'.

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/ward's line mid intro
speaker: Mister Ward

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/doyle tells about breakfast
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: Em...

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/doyle tells about breakfast
speaker: Mister Doyle
en: This might be a good time to mention that breakfast will be ready at 9am in case anyone wants to return to their rooms and freshen up?

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/doyle tells about breakfast

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/ward notices quinn
speaker: Mister Ward

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/ward notices quinn

conversation: Ground floor/Saloon/quinn asks about ward

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from Ward/Chess game

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from Ward/Bookshelves

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from Ward/Chalkboard

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from Ward/Vase

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from Ward/Hearth

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from Ward/Suit of armour
speaker: Mister Ward

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from Ward/bookshelf with bible
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Many books but nothing stands ou-- hold up, what's this?

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from Ward/bookshelf with bible

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from Ward/bookshelf with bible

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from Ward/records

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from Ward/records

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from Ward/gramophone

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from Ward/take sleep record

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from Ward/take sleep record

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from Ward/record onto gramophone

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from Ward/record off gramophone

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from Ward/quinn book

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from Ward/quinn book

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Well, here, thank you all for coming to listen to me talk. I hear a lot of you have come from far afield...

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: So it seems only right that you should get to know this place, our home, a little better.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: We share this land with the Other Crowd, the Aos Sí, or People of the Mound. You'll have heard them called many things, no doubt...

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: When mankind settled this land, they made a deal with the Fair Folk; they would take half the land, and the Fair Folk would take the other.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Humanity, being tricky, chose the upper half, and now the Fair Folk live in the Otherworld, parallel to this one.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Still, there's nothing to stop the Aos Sí from walking among us, and they often do. You'd always do best to mind them, and be polite to them.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: ...Otherwise, they might well cause you trouble. Many have learned the Aos Sí don't take slights kindly, and can give you the worst sort of luck.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Of course, the fair folk have to have means to reach us, and there are plenty of gateways between this world and theirs.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: But they don't all bring bad luck. Some are only mischievous; some mean well; and some might be bad omens, but they only serve to warn us of ill fate.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: It's not uncommon to find a tree left out in the middle of a farmer's field. Lone hawthorn trees are the meeting place between our world and theirs.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: It's an terrible offence to disturb one, and people know better than to try. There are some things in this land that should, by all accounts, be left alone...

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Thank you all for coming. I hear a lot of you have come from far afield...

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: The fair folk have the means to reach us, and there are plenty of gateways between this world and theirs.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: So, now we share the land with the Aos Sí, the fae - or sometimes, as we call them, the Fair Folk. And while they often live apart from us...

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: So there's nothing to stop the Aos Sí from walking among us, and they often do. You'd always do best to mind them, and be polite to them.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: ...Otherwise, they might well cause you trouble. Many have learned the Aos Sí don't take slights kindly, and can give you the worst sort of luck.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: They don't all bring bad luck. Some are only mischievous; some mean well; and some might be bad omens, but they only serve to warn us of ill fate.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Either way, they are best left undisturbed. They are one of many things in this land that are not to be meddled with.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: To those of you I haven't met, I'm Fiadh Callaghan, and I'm here to talk to you all about the 'Other Crowd'.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ STAY AND LISTEN]

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ LEAVE ]

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Mister Ward
en: If you'll excuse me...

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Well, this is more of a turnout than I was expecting!

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Right. No more questions. I'm tired of trying to talk sense into you lot. Listen or don't. It's no skin off my nose.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Mister Toussaint
en: And these fairie--

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: --please, Sir, don't call them that. I've given you many's an alternative that won't draw their eye to this place. Which you don't want, trust me there.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Mister Toussaint
en: My apologies, Madame. These Other Folk, they differ from the winged fairies of children's stories, oui?

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: As much as you and I differ from a wild animal, yes.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: All of Europe - probably further - has their own form of the Good Folk. Primordial forces of nature, all. As unknowable to us as a storm or wave.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: As I said, Catholic monks came and tainted history. Tried to write them out of existence, and when that failed, they tried to write the fear out of them.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Stories are powerful ways to change a land and its power. It's why the church always folded in the rituals and beliefs of a place they came to.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: We saw it again in the invasion of the Americas...

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Ah, look, I've lost my train of thought with all your questions. Where was I?

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Writing them as friendly winged sprites, friendly to children and all that.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Barbosa
en: "Write the fear out of them" - what does this mean?

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: And what are they?

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Sure, I can't tell you what nobody knows.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: But they are more than that... some would say they are the land incarnate.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Really, it's best to think of them as forces of nature.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: They are no more good or evil than a storm. But, you'd also want to stay out of the path of a bad storm.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: All that said, it's easier to avoid a storm - there are signs and you get warning. Not so with the Other Folk; best you can do is be polite and leave your offerings.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: And to avoid them altogether? Best not to meddle in anything that might catch their eye.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: That's the main reason we don't call them by their name. Or, you know, do strange magic on their doorstep...

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: The church would tie themselves in knots trying to bend the truths of the world to fit their narrative...

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: They want you to believe, first of all, that the Other Crowd don't exist. Then secondly, once you know they are real, the Church wants you to think of them as angels - ones that never took a side in the battle of Heaven.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Cast down to Earth and not Hell for their sitting on the fence. Now - I've never heard anything of this ilk from any reliable source, only holy salesmen.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Other people confuse them for types of ghosts. And given how similar the bean sídhe and fear gorta are to ghosts, I can forgive that.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: What else... Oh yes - speaking of Samhain... Masks!

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: You all have costumes for the ball this evening, yes?

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: It is all good fun, Sì? My outfit will amaze!

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Well, yes. But also... no...

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Samhain is when the dead walk among us. You know this - sure you're here for that, right?

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Well, when they leave, they don't always leave empty-handed. Some want to drag the living with them, jealous as they are.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Maybe. It's certainly been said before. But just this one year... this one year when you're pushing the barriers to their limits, you might do well to keep a superstition or two in your back pocket.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: That's why we dress up as ghoulish figures  - so they can’t tell the difference between us and them, and will leave us be.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: ...I can see some of your faces - superstitious old bat, you're thinking.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: ...the Good People, the Wee Folk, the Fair Folk. Some of you will know them by the F-word, but we won't be saying that here.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Fiadh's Other Crowd Talk
speaker: Miss Callaghan
en: Like in our case, how Ostara became Easter, Yule became Christmas, and Samhain became All Souls Day when the blessing of the graves gets done.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: There is still much we don't know about ghosts, you must think? And this is true - yet there is plenty to speak on, so do not worry! *cough*

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: By their nature... ghosts are hard to find and define. And yet, even in their... elusive... ness... Questo funzionerà... we find them everywhere.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: By their many names, they are all across the world. They are known all across the world. And how could they not be?

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: For whatever we may call them - ghosts, phantoms, or spirits - there is more to this world than meets the eye, and that is true everywhere you go.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: There are many formations of what we call ghosts, but mostly, when they are on this side of the veil, we see them in a few forms particularly...

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: So, tomorrow, when the veil is at its thinnest... mind your words. These spirits were once people. They are their intangible remains...

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: And they will be just as driven as they ever were, if not more.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: We understand ghosts to be the disembodied souls of their old selves, sometimes less, or incomplete, as to how they were before.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: Or, if not thinking souls, the imprints of great grief *cough* or strife left upon the world.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: ...So, grazie mille, for attending. Now - I will speak with you about ghosts. Spirits! Phantoms!

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: Ciao, ciao! For those of you I have not yet had the pleasure of meeting, I am Carmela Mantovani. And I am here to talk about ghosts and all that we know of them.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ STAY AND LISTEN ]

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ LEAVE ]

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Mister Ward
en: If you'll excuse me...

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: So, why do I have such hopes for this séance?

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: This, I have been doing for a long time. When you invite a ghost to speak with you, there are always limits.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: The strength of the spirit, the skill of the medium, the thickness of the veil... All of these things can make it difficult for a ghost to manifest.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: We see their forms on occasion, we feel the echoes of their emotion, but these things do not require expense. They sustain themselves. Somehow. This we do not understand.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: It takes effort for a spirit to be more than echoes, to make a more conscious connection with the world of the living.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: By their nature, they are hard to define. And yet, even in their... elusive... ness... Questo funzionerà... we find them everywhere!

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: By their many names, they are all across the world. There are many formations...

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: Some echo the grief they left upon the world and are blind to the living. *cough*

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: While others are vengeful and aggressive, haunting a person or place and causing everything from psychological to physical damage!

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: Regardless. No single spectre has been able to directly communicate.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: But tomorrow night - ah, tomorrow night we intend to change this!

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: So, what stops them from speaking? Is it a physical matter? No, it cannot be, as they interact with the world in other ways.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: Blowing papers off desks, snuffing candles, sometimes even striking people. *cough* *cough*

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: Perhaps the limitation is in their lungs, then? Well, no, many wail and moan after all.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: Maybe they simply cannot speak for themselves?

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: Could it be they have nothing to say?

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: I do not think so. Many a mystic, myself included, believe that spirits have given us a feeling of things they want said.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: There is a chance this is wishful thinking on our parts, but I believe so many have felt this that at least one person must be correct...

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: This, we cannot rule out, and is to be my conclusion if our séance does not bear fruit.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: We think of ghosts as waveforms. Spiritual waveforms. A soul rippling long past the death of its host, its shell.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: They are in a frequency we cannot easily see. In daytime, they are almost invisible to us.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: This is an *cough* age of science, yes? So let me speak in those terms.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: At night, easier to see. The less... interference around - lights, other people, and so on - the easier, still.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: If you have noticed animals behaving strangely, this is because they see different wavelengths to us, as is with light.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: The atmosphere blocks the wavelength of light. The same is true for spiritual wavelengths.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: But at this time of year, the veil - or spiritual atmosphere - is at its thinnest.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: And this place is reported to have many ghosts. So our wavelengths have less distance to travel and less to block them.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: And then, there is you. Those gathered. People attuned to the mystical, coming together to work as a... qual è la parola? A net to catch the signal.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: No, net is not correct. Che cos'è? Ah, my words let me down. But look, if you do not believe me?

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: I'm told that crows are a symbol of your Irish death-goddess. They are gathering! And at night, the dead are roaming - I think they line up for the chance to speak to us!

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: In parting, a warning.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: We do know that not all dead linger - only those bound to a place, an object, a person stay. Why? This, eh, this we do not know yet for certain.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: It is theorised that all spirits are bound, fettered, by an emotional component - death in a place, obsession with an object, love or anger to a person.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: And then, there is you. Those gathered. Do I describe you as a way to boost the wavelength or as a way to widen the signal receiver?

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: I do not know, but the effect is the same. And if you don't believe me?

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Carmela's Ghosts talk
speaker: Miss Mantovani
en: I'm told that crows are a symbol of The Morrigan, the Irish death-goddess. They are gathering! And at night the dead are roaming - I think they line up for the chance to speak to us!

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: Well. This is quite the turnout. Even the Marquess himself has come. Well...

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: I hadn't expected anyone to take much interest in the area.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: I suppose I should start by introducing myself. My name is Simon Coventry.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: I'm going to share some interesting facts about this part of Ireland that I picked up while researching for this trip.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ STAY AND LISTEN ]

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ LEAVE ]

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Mister Ward
en: Please excuse me.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: So, I am sure you all know this land came into the Blake family in the 1650s after Cromwell's invasion.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: What I found interesting was what came before...

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: This land was a place of worship and innovation.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: I couldn't find anything that spoke to what happened at the work from that site - presumably it was set ablaze.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: One has to assume not everyone was put to death by Cromwell's forces, however...

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: I suspect many surrounding families have stories and knowledge passed down from that time and those people.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: Why, given his background, perhaps our very own Doctor Callaghan is linked to that place?

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Doctor Callaghan
en: Ha, you flatter me, Sir.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: Does anything of the pre-Christian site still exist?

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Father Sinnott
en: I read one monk's account that what was here before was partially underground.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: There are some sinkholes on the far reaches of the grounds, where caverns beneath the old settlements collapsed in.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I do not know whether those collapses are the result of time or if they were manually closed.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I suppose it matters not either way. Nothing else remains.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: That's me, I am afraid. I've nothing else to share.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: Probably quite mundane in the face of everything, but nothing wrong with a break in the face of madness!

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: Perhaps those survivors are the reason that Connacht is home to all manner of wonderful myths and sacred sites?

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: Rathcroghan and Oweynagat cave, Queen Medb and her cattle raids, the Children of Lir - all fascinating stories, but too long to get into here.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: A gathering spot for scholars and engineers, and artists to work on understanding and advancement - the betterment of their people.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: Easy pickings for Edward Blake. No doubt he and Cromwell cared very little for any knowledge held by 'primitive pagans'...

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Missus D'Arcy
en: Thank you Marquess. I wanted to ask about the land before your family came here - is it true this was a sacred site?

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Before my family brought culture and civilisation, Sir, every tree, stone, and river was sacred to the savage pagans of these lands.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: But you are right, this was a place of particular significance.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: It was said to be home to their god of innovation and medicine.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: It brought many of their finest minds to the area, whatever bar for quality that could mean.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I suspect this played large part in Cromwell ordering it raised to the ground and built over. As both a statement and to consecrate the land in God's glory.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Mister Skerritt
en: Perhaps things would have turned out better for them had this been a shrine to ones of their war gods, eh? Hahaha!

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: ...indeed.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: I could find no knowledge of what happened to any of the work from that site, presumably it was set ablaze.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: Oh... I don't think so, I am afraid. From what I can gather, it was all razed to make way for the castle and its estate.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: Well! There you go, Father.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: You've done your homework, Father. Yes, some accounts do suggest that - though none of the maps I've studied show anything useful. Marquess?

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/coventry on the region
speaker: Mister Coventry
en: Certainly worth a read in the very well-stocked library here, if you find yourself bored - not that I can see that happening with the séance only hours away!

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Blake on blake manor
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Of course, the Great Famine was hard on much of Ireland.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Blake on blake manor
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: And we were no exception.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Blake on blake manor
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Those were hard years on the land and our family.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Blake on blake manor
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: My father sold much of the estate and made some... daring investments across Europe.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Blake on blake manor
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: They did not pay off.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Blake on blake manor
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: And so, when I was of age and title, I turned the manor into a hotel.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Blake on blake manor
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: What remains of the land is still farmed or forested, of course.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Blake on blake manor
speaker: Mister Ward
en: If you'll excuse me...

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Blake on blake manor
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Welcome, all of you, to my home. I am Jonathan Blake, the Marquess of Doon, lord of this manor, and all the land that can be seen from it.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Blake on blake manor
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I have been asked to speak with you about the house and its history, which dates back to 1652.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Blake on blake manor
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ STAY AND LISTEN]

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Blake on blake manor
speaker: Detective Ward
en: [ LEAVE ]

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Blake on blake manor
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: My ancestor, Edward Blake, was granted this land in the winter of 1651. The following summer, work began on the castle that, in turn, became this manor.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Blake on blake manor
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: You Sir, a question?

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Blake on blake manor
speaker: Mister Skerritt
en: Thank you, Marquess. Not to turn things gruesome, but is it true? What they say about the walled-up rooms?

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Blake on blake manor
speaker: Marquess Blake

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Blake on blake manor
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: As such we continue to display a portrait of Percival Blake. That said, I did have it moved from the main halls on the staff's request. Now it is in one of the towers, though I can't recall which.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Blake on blake manor
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Certainly, it is rumoured that Percival Blake bricked away two young lovers for angering him.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Blake on blake manor
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Set across from one another, so they could hear each other's final days.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Blake on blake manor
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: That said, no such chambers were found, nor records of work being done that match the timing.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Blake on blake manor
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: It is true that a young couple did indeed vanish with no record, but that wasn't uncommon for that era.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Blake on blake manor
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Over the years, some staff, and yes, even guests, have reported hearing sobs from a young woman in the east of the manor. But given the lack of evidence, these are likely flights of fancy.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Blake on blake manor
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: The building has been expanded many times over since then, and you would be hard-pressed to tell the original building and the additions apart.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Blake on blake manor
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: But the main compound has roughly expanded to five times its original size. This is not counting the basement, which was added in the late 1700s.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Blake on blake manor
speaker: Missus D'Arcy
en: Thank you Marquess. Any more tragic deaths to share?

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Blake on blake manor
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: ...No more questions? Okay. Let us conclude then. Thank you all for your time.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Blake on blake manor
speaker: Miss Hisham
en: Ya lahwi...

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Blake on blake manor
speaker: Marquess Blake

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Blake on blake manor
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I'm not sure this place has any more tragedy than any other family in this land.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Blake on blake manor
speaker: Missus D'Arcy
en: Then why all the ghost stories? I don't think we all gathered here for no reason...

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Blake on blake manor
speaker: Marquess Blake

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Blake on blake manor
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: Spending too much time digging around in our library, eh Mister Skerritt?

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Blake on blake manor
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: ...all death is tragic, Missus D'Arcy.

conversation: Ground floor/Drawing Room/comments from NPCs/Blake on blake manor
speaker: Marquess Blake
en: I shall take my leave, but I hope you enjoy the rest of your stay here at Blake Manor.
